6.9: And there is a friend, who being turned to enmitie, and strife, will discouer thy reproch.
6.10: Againe some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of thy affliction.
6.11: But in thy prosperitie hee will be as thy selfe, and will be bould ouer thy seruants.
6.12: If thou be brought low, he will be against thee, and will hide himselfe from thy face.
6.13: Separate thy selfe from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends.
6.14: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and hee that hath found such an one, hath found a treasure.
6.15: Nothing doeth counteruaile a faithful friend, and his excellencie is vnualuable.
6.16: A faithfull friend is the medicine of life, and they that feare the Lord shal finde him.
6.17: Who so feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright, for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
6.18: My sonne, gather instruction from thy youth vp: so shalt thou finde wisedome till thine old age.
6.19: Come vnto her as one that ploweth, and soweth, and wait for her good fruits, for thou shalt not toile much in labouring about her, but thou shalt eat of her fruits right soone.
6.20: She is very vnpleasant to the vnlearned: he that is without vnderstanding, will not remaine with her.
6.21: She wil lye vpon him as a mightie stone of triall, and hee will cast her from him ere it be long.
6.22: For wisedome is according to her name, and she is not manifest vnto many.
6.23: Giue eare, my sonne, receiue my aduice, and refuse not my counsell,
6.24: And put thy feet into her fetters, and thy necke into her chaine.
6.25: Bow downe thy shoulder, and beare her, and be not grieued with her bonds.
6.26: Come vnto her with thy whole heart, and keepe her wayes with all thy power.
6.27: Search and seeke, and shee shall bee made knowen vnto thee, and when thou hast got hold of her, let her not goe.
6.28: For at the last thou shalt finde her rest, and that shalbe turned to thy ioy.
6.29: Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for thee, and her chaines a robe of glory.
6.30: For there is a golden ornament vpon her, and her bandes are purple lace.
6.31: Thou shalt put her on as a robe of honour: and shalt put her about thee as a crowne of ioy.
6.32: My sonne, if thou wilt, thou shalt bee taught: and if thou wilt apply thy minde, thou shalt be prudent.
6.33: If thou loue to heare, thou shalt receiue vnderstanding: and if thou bow thine eare, thou shalt be wise.
6.34: Stand in the multitude of the elders, and cleaue vnto him that is wise.
6.35: Be willing to heare euery godly discourse, and let not the parables of vnderstanding escape thee.
6.36: And if thou seest a man of vnderstanding, get thee betimes vnto him, and let thy foote weare the steps of his doore.
6.37: Let thy minde be vpon the ordinances of the Lord, & meditate continually in his commandements: he shal establish thine heart, and giue thee wisedome at thine owne desire.

7.1: Doe no euill, so shall no harme come vnto thee.
7.2: Depart from the vniust, and iniquitie shall turne away from thee.
7.3: My sonne, sow not vpon the furrowes of vnrighteousnesse, and thou shalt not reape them seuen folde.
7.4: Seeke not of the Lord preheminence, neither of the King the seate of honour.
7.5: Iustifie not thy selfe before the Lord, and boast not of thy wisedome before the king.
7.6: Seeke not to be iudge, being not able to take away iniquitie, lest at any time thou feare the person of the mightie, and lay a stumbling blocke in the way of thy vprightnesse.
7.7: Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then thou shalt not cast thy selfe downe among the people.
7.8: Bind not one sinne vpon another, for in one thou shalt not be vnpunished.
7.9: Say not, God wil looke vpon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most High God, he will accept it.
7.10: Be not faint hearted when thou makest thy prayer, and neglect not to giue almes.
7.11: Laugh no man to scorne in the bitternesse of his soule: for there is one which humbleth and exalteth.
7.12: Deuise not a lie against thy brother: neither doe the like to thy friend.
7.13: Use not to make any maner of lie: for the custome thereof is not good.
7.14: Use not many words in a multitude of Elders, and make not much babling when thou prayest.
7.15: Hate not laborious worke, neither husbandrie, which the most High hath ordeined.
7.16: Number not thy selfe among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tary long.
7.17: Humble thy soule greatly: for the vengeance of the vngodly is fire and wormes.
7.18: Change not a friend for any good by no meanes: neither a faithfull brother for the gold of Ophir.
7.19: Forgoe not a wise and good woman: for her grace is aboue gold.
7.20: Whereas thy seruant worketh truely, entreate him not euill, nor the hireling that bestoweth himselfe wholly for thee.
7.21: Let thy soule loue a good seruant, and defraud him not of liberty.
7.22: Hast thou cattell? haue an eye to them, and if they be for thy profit, keepe them with thee.
7.23: Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow downe their necke from their youth.
7.24: Hast thou daughters? haue care of their body, and shewe not thy selfe cheerefull toward them.
7.25: Marrie thy daughter, and so shalt thou haue performed a weightie matter: but giue her to a man of vnderstanding.
7.26: Hast thou a wife after thy minde? forsake her not, but giue not thy selfe ouer to a light woman.
7.27: Honour thy father with thy whole heart, and forget not the sorrowes of thy mother.
7.28: Remember that thou wast begot of them, and how canst thou recompense them the things that they haue done for thee?
7.29: Feare the Lord with all thy soule, and reuerence his priests.
7.30: Loue him that made thee with all thy strength, and forsake not his ministers.
7.31: Feare the Lord, and honour the priest: and giue him his portion, as it is commanded thee, the first fruits, and the trespasse offering, & the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things.
7.32: And stretch thine hand vnto the poore, that thy blessing may be perfected
7.33: A gift hath grace in the sight of euery man liuing, and for the dead deteine it not.
7.34: Faile not to bee with them that weepe, and mourne with them that mourne.
7.35: Be not slow to visit the sicke: for that shall make thee to be beloued.
7.36: Whatsoeuer thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt neuer doe amisse.

8.1: Striue not with a mighty man, lest thou fall into his hands.
8.2: Bee not at variance with a rich man, lest he ouerweigh thee: for gold hath destroyed many, and peruerted the hearts of kings.
8.3: Striue not with a man that is full of tongue, and heape not wood vpon his fire.
8.4: Iest not with a rude man, lest thy ancestours be disgraced.
8.5: Reproch not a man that turneth from sinne, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
8.6: Dishonour not a man in his old age: for euen some of vs waxe old.
8.7: Reioice not ouer thy greatest enemie being dead, but remember that we die all.
8.8: Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thy selfe with their prouerbs; for of them thou shalt learne instruction, & how to serue great men with ease.
8.9: Misse not the discourse of the Elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them thou shalt learne vnderstanding, and to giue answere as need requireth.
8.10: Kindle not the coales of a sinner, lest thou be burnt with the flame of his fire.
8.11: Rise not vp (in anger) at the presence of an iniurious person, least he lie in waite to entrap thee in thy words.
8.12: Lend not vnto him that is mightier then thy selfe; for if thou lendest him, count it but lost.
8.13: Be not surety aboue thy power: for if thou be surety, take care to pay it.
8.14: Goe not to law with a iudge, for they will iudge for him according to his honour.
8.15: Trauaile not by the way with a bold fellow, least he become grieuous vnto thee: for he will doe according to his owne will, and thou shalt perish with him through his folly.
8.16: Striue not with an angry man, and goe not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no helpe, he will ouerthrow thee.
8.17: Consult not with a foole; for he cannot keepe counsell.
8.18: Doe no secret thing before a stranger, for thou knowest not what he will bring forth.
8.19: Open not thine heart to euery man, least he requite thee with a shrewd turne.

9.1: Be not iealous ouer the wife of thy bosome, and teach her not an euil lesson against thy selfe.
9.2: Giue not thy soule vnto a woman, to set her foot vpon thy substance.
9.3: Meete not with an harlot, least thou fall into her snares.
9.4: Use not much the companie of a woman that is a singer, least thou be taken with her attempts.
9.5: Gaze not on a maide, that thou fall not by those things, that are pretious in her.
9.6: Giue not thy soule vnto harlots, that thou loose not thine inheritance.
9.7: Looke not round about thee, in the streets of the citie, neither wander thou in the solitary places thereof.
9.8: Turne away thine eye from a beautifull woman, and looke not vpon anothers beautie: for many haue beene deceiued by the beautie of a woman, for heerewith loue is kindled as a fire.
9.9: Sit not at all with another mans wife, nor sit downe with her in thine armes, and spend not thy money with her at the wine, least thine heart incline vnto her, and so thorough thy desire thou fall into destruction.
9.10: Forsake not an old friend, for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine: when it is old, thou shalt drinke it with pleasure.
9.11: Enuy not the glory of a sinner: for thou knowest not what shall be his end.
9.12: Delight not in the thing that the vngodly haue pleasure in, but remember they shall not goe vnpunished vnto their graue.
9.13: Keepe thee farre from the man that hath power to kill, so shalt thou not doubt the feare of death: and if thou come vnto him, make no fault, least he take away thy life presently: remember that thou goest in the midst of snares, and that thou walkest vpon the battlements of the citie.
9.14: As neere as thou canst, ghesse at thy neighbour, and consult with the wise.
9.15: Let thy talke be with the wise, and all thy communication in the law of the most high.
9.16: And let iust men eate and drinke with thee, and let thy glorying be in the feare of the Lord.
9.17: For the hand of the artificer, the worke shall be commended: and the wise ruler of the people, for his speech.
9.18: A man of an ill tongue is dangerous in his citie, and he that is rash in his talke shall be hated.

10.1: A wise iudge will instruct his people, & the gouernement of a prudent man is well ordered.
10.2: As the iudge of the people is himselfe, so are his officers, and what maner of man the ruler of the citie is, such are all they that dwell therein.
10.3: An vnwise king destroyeth his people, but through the prudence of them which are in authoritie, the citie shalbe inhabited.
10.4: The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time hee will set ouer it one that is profitable.
10.5: In the hand of God is the prosperitie of man: and vpon the person of the scribe shall he lay his honour.
10.6: Beare not hatred to thy neighbour for euery wrong, and do nothing at all by iniurious practises.
10.7: Pride is hatefull before God, and man: and by both doeth one commit iniquitie.
10.8: Because of vnrighteous dealings, iniuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdome is translated from one people to another.
10.9: Why is earth and ashes proude? There is not a more wicked thing, then a couetous man: for such an one setteth his owne soule to sale, because while he liueth, he casteth away his bowels.
10.10: The Phisition cutteth off a long disease, and he that is to day a King, to morrow shall die.
10.11: For when a man is dead, hee shall inherite creeping things, beastes and wormes.
10.12: The beginning of pride is, when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his maker.
10.13: For pride is the beginning of sinne, and hee that hath it, shall powre out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought vpon them strange calamities, and ouerthrew them vtterly.
10.14: The Lord hath cast downe the thrones of proud Princes, and set vp the meeke in their stead.
10.15: The Lord hath plucked vp the rootes of the proud nations: and planted the lowly in their place.
10.16: The Lord ouerthrew countreys of the heathen: and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
10.17: He tooke some of them away, and destroyed them, and hath made their memoriall to cease from the earth.
10.18: Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are borne of a woman.
10.19: They that feare the Lord are a sure seed, and they that loue him, an honourable plant: they that regard not the Law, are a dishonourable seed, they that transgresse the commandements, are a deceiuable seed.
10.20: Among brethren he that is chiefe is honourable, so are they that feare the Lord in his eyes.
10.21: The feare of the Lord goeth before the obtayning of authoritie: but roughnesse and pride, is the loosing thereof.
10.22: Whether hee bee rich, noble, or poore, their glorie is the feare of the Lord.
10.23: It is not meet to despise the poore man that hath vnderstanding, neither is it conuenient to magnifie a sinnefull man.
10.24: Great men, and Iudges, and Potentates shall bee honoured, yet is there none of them greater then he that feareth the Lord.
10.25: Unto the seruant that is wise, shall they that are free doe seruice: and hee that hath knowledge, will not grudge when he is reformed.
10.26: Be not ouerwise in doing thy busines, and boast not thy selfe in the time of thy distresse.
10.27: Better is he that laboureth and aboundeth in all things, then hee that boasteth himselfe, and wanteth bread.
10.28: My sonne, glorifie thy soule in meekenesse, and giue it honour according to the dignitie thereof.
10.29: Who wil iustifie him that sinneth against his owne soule? and who will honour him that dishonoureth his owne life?
10.30: The poore man is honoured for his skill, and the rich man is honoured for his riches.
10.31: Hee that is honoured in pouertie, how much more in riches? And he that is dishonourable in riches, how much more in pouertie?

11.1: Wisedome lifteth vp the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men.
11.2: Commend not a man for his beautie, neither abhorre a man for his outward appearance.
11.3: The Bee is little among such as flie, but her fruite is the chiefe of sweete things.
11.4: Boast not of thy cloathing and raiment, and exalt not thy selfe in the day of honour: for the workes of the Lord are wonderfull, and his workes among men are hidden.
11.5: Many kings haue sit downe vpon the ground, and one that was neuer thought of, hath worne the crowne.
11.6: Many mightie men haue beene greatly disgraced: and the honourable deliuered into other mens hands.
11.7: Blame not before thou hast examined the trueth: vnderstand first, and then rebuke.
11.8: Answere not, before thou hast heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talke.
11.9: Striue not in a matter that concerneth thee not: and sit not in iudgement with sinners.
11.10: My sonne, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent: and if thou follow after, thou shalt not obtaine, neither shalt thou escape by flying.
11.11: There is one that laboureth and taketh paines, and maketh haste, and is so much the more behinde.
11.12: Againe, there is another that is slow, and hath neede of helpe, wanting abilitie, and full of pouertie, yet the eye of the Lord looked vpon him for good, and set him vp from his low estate,
11.13: And lifted vp his head from miserie, so that many that saw it, marueiled at him.
11.14: Prosperitie and aduersitie, life and death, pouerty and riches, come of the Lord.
11.15: Wisedome, knowledge, and vnderstanding of the Lawe, are of the Lord: loue, & the way of good workes, are from him.
11.16: Errour and darkenesse had their beginning together with sinners: and euill shall waxe old with them that glory therein.
11.17: The gift of the Lord remaineth with the godly, and his fauour bringeth prosperitie for euer.
11.18: There is that waxeth rich by his warinesse, and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:
11.19: Whereas he sayth, I haue found rest, and now will eate continually of my goods, and yet hee knoweth not what time shall come vpon him, and that hee must leaue those things to others, and die.
11.20: Be stedfast in thy couenant, and be conuersant therein, and waxe olde in thy worke.
11.21: Marueile not at the workes of sinners, but trust in the Lord, and abide in thy labour: for it is an easie thing in the sight of the Lord, on the sudden to make a poore man rich.
11.22: The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly, and suddenly he maketh his blessing to flourish.
11.23: Say not, what profit is there of my seruice? and what good things shal I haue hereafter?
11.24: Againe, say not, I haue enough, and possesse many things; and what euill can come to me hereafter?
11.25: In the day of prosperitie, there is a forgetfulnesse of affliction: and in the day of affliction, there is no remembrance of prosperitie.
11.26: For it is an easie thing vnto the Lord in the day of death, to reward a man according to his wayes.
11.27: The affliction of an houre, maketh a man forget pleasure: and in his end, his deeds shalbe discouered.
11.28: Iudge none blessed before his death: for a man shall bee knowen in his children.
11.29: Bring not euery man into thine house, for the deceitfull man hath many traines.
11.30: Like as a Partrich taken in a cage, so is the heart of the proud; and like as a spie, watcheth hee for thy fall.
11.31: For hee lieth in wait, and turneth good into euill, and in things worthy praise, will lay blame vpon thee.
11.32: Of a sparke of fire, a heape of coales is kindled: and a sinnefull man layeth waite for blood.
11.33: Take heed of a mischieuous man, (for hee worketh wickednesse) lest hee bring vpon thee a perpetuall blot.
11.34: Receiue a stranger into thine house, and hee will disturbe thee, and turne thee out of thine owne.

12.1: When thou wilt doe good, know to whō thou doest it, so shalt thou be thanked for thy benefites.
12.2: Do good to the godly man, and thou shalt find a recompence, and if not from him, yet from the most high.
12.3: There can no good come to him that is alwayes occupied in euill: nor to him that giueth no almes.
12.4: Giue to the godly man, and helpe not a sinner.
12.5: Doe well vnto him that is lowly, but giue not to the vngodly: hold backe thy bread, and giue it not vnto him, lest he ouermaster thee thereby. For thou shalt receiue twice as much euill, for all the good thou shalt haue done vnto him.
12.6: For the most High hateth sinners, and will repay vengeance vnto the vngodly, and keepeth them against the mightie day of their punishment.
12.7: Giue vnto the good, and helpe not the sinner.
12.8: A friend cannot be knowen in prosperitie, and an enemy cannot be hidden in aduersitie.
12.9: In the prosperitie of a man, enemies will be grieued, but in his aduersitie, euen a friend will depart.
12.10: Neuer trust thine enemie: for like as yron rusteth, so is his wickednesse.
12.11: Though he humble himselfe, and goe crouching, yet take good heed, and beware of him, and thou shalt bee vnto him, as if thou hadst wiped a looking glasse, and thou shalt knowe that his rust hath not beene altogether wiped away.
12.12: Set him not by thee, lest when he hath ouerthrowen thee, he stand vp in thy place, neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seeke to take thy seat, and thou at the last remember my wordes, and be pricked therewith.
12.13: Who will pitie a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, or any such as come nigh wilde beasts?
12.14: So one that goeth to a sinner, and is defiled with him in his sinnes, who will pitie?
12.15: For a while hee will abide with thee, but if thou begin to fall, he wil not tarie.
12.16: An enemie speaketh sweetly with his lippes, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw thee into a pit: hee will weepe with his eyes, but if he find opportunitie, hee will not be satisfied with blood.
12.17: If aduersitie come vpon thee, thou shalt find him there first, & though he pretend to helpe thee, yet shal he vndermine thee.
12.18: He will shake his head and clap his handes, and whisper much, and change his countenance.

13.1: He that toucheth pitch, shal be defiled therewith, and hee that hath fellowship with a proude man, shall be like vnto him.
13.2: Burthen not thy selfe aboue thy power, while thou liuest, and haue no fellowship with one that is mightier, and richer then thy selfe. For how agree the kettle and the earthen pot together? for if the one be smitten against the other, it shall be broken.
13.3: The rich man hath done wrong, and yet he threatneth withall: the poore is wronged, and he must intreat also.
13.4: If thou be for his profit, he will vse thee: but if thou haue nothing, he will forsake thee.
13.5: If thou haue any thing, he will liue with thee, yea he will make thee bare, and will not be sorie for it.
13.6: If he haue need of thee, hee will deceiue thee, and smile vpon thee, and put thee in hope, he will speake thee faire, and say, What wantest thou?
13.7: And hee will shame thee by his meates, vntill he haue drawen thee drie twice or thrice, and at the last hee will laugh thee to scorne: afterward when he seeth thee, he will forsake thee, and shake his head at thee.
13.8: Beware that thou bee not deceiued, and brought downe in thy iolitie.
13.9: If thou be inuited of a mighty man, withdraw thy selfe, and so much the more will he inuite thee.
13.10: Presse thou not vpon him, lest thou be put backe, stand not farre off, lest thou be forgotten.
13.11: Affect not to be made equall vnto him in talke, and beleeue not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt thee, and smiling vpon thee will get out thy secrets.
13.12: But cruelly he will lay vp thy words, and will not spare to doe thee hurt, and to put thee in prison.
13.13: Obserue and take good heed, for thou walkest in peril of thy ouerthrowing: when thou hearest these things, awake in thy sleepe.
13.14: Loue the Lord all thy life, and call vpon him for thy saluation.
13.15: Euery beast loueth his like, and euery man loueth his neighbour.
13.16: All flesh consorteth according to kind, and a man will cleaue to his like:
13.17: What fellowship hath the wolfe with the lambe? so the sinner with the godly.
13.18: What agreement is there betweene the Hyena and a dogge? and what peace betweene the rich and the poore?
13.19: As the wilde asse is the lyons pray in the wildernesse: so the rich eate vp the poore.
13.20: As the proud hate humilitie: so doth the rich abhorre the poore.
13.21: A rich man beginning to fall, is held vp of his friends: but a poore man being downe, is thrust also away by his friends.
13.22: When a rich man is fallen, he hath many helpers: he speaketh things not to be spoken, and yet men iustifie him: the poore man slipt, and yet they rebuked him too: he spake wisely, and could haue no place.
13.23: When a rich man speaketh, euery man holdeth his tongue, and looke what hee sayeth, they extoll it to the clouds: but if the poore man speake, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will helpe to ouerthrowe him.
13.24: Riches are good vnto him that hath no sinne, and pouerty is euill in the mouth of the vngodly.
13.25: The heart of a man changeth his countenance, whether it be for good or euill: and a merry heart maketh a cheerefull countenance.
13.26: A cheerefull countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity, and the finding out of parables, is a wearisome labour of the minde.

14.1: Blessed is the man that hath not slipt with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sinnes.
14.2: Blessed is hee whose conscience hath not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in the Lord.
14.3: Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an enuious man doe with money?
14.4: He that gathereth by defrauding his owne soule, gathereth for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
14.5: Hee that is euill to himselfe, to whom will he be good? he shall not take pleasure in his goods.
14.6: There is none worse then he that enuieth himselfe; and this is a recompence of his wickednesse.
14.7: And if he doth good, he doth it vnwillingly, and at the last he will declare his wickednesse.
14.8: The enuious man hath a wicked eye, he turneth away his face and despiseth men.
14.9: A couetous mans eye is not satisfied with his portion, and the iniquity of the wicked dryeth vp his soule.
14.10: A wicked eye enuieth bread, and he is a niggard at his table.
14.11: My sonne, according to thy habilitie doe good to thy selfe, and giue the Lord his due offering.
14.12: Remember that death will not be long in comming, and that the couenant of the graue is not shewed vnto thee.
14.13: Doe good vnto thy friend before thou die, and according to thy abilitie, stretch out thy hand and giue to him.
14.14: Defraud not thy selfe of the good day, and let not the part of a good desire ouerpasse thee.
14.15: Shalt thou not leaue thy trauailes vnto another? and thy labours to be diuided by lot?
14.16: Giue, and take, and sanctifie thy soule, for there is no seeking of dainties in the graue.
14.17: All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the couenant from the beginning is; thou shalt die the death.
14.18: As of the greene leaues on a thicke tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one commeth to an end, and another is borne.
14.19: Euery worke rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker therof shal goe withall.
14.20: Blessed is the man that doeth meditate good things in wisdome, and that reasoneth of holy things by his vnderstanding.
14.21: He that considereth her wayes in his heart, shall also haue vnderstanding in her secrets.
14.22: Goe after her as one that traceth, and lie in wait in her wayes.
14.23: Hee that prieth in at her windowes, shal also hearken at her doores.
14.24: Hee that doeth lodge neere her house, shall also fasten a pin in her walles.
14.25: He shall pitch his tent nigh vnto her, and shall lodge in a lodging where good things are.
14.26: He shal set his children vnder her shelter, and shall lodge vnder her branches.
14.27: By her he shall be couered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.

15.1: He that feareth the Lord will doe good, and he that hath the knowledge of the Law shal obtaine her.
15.2: And as a mother shall she meet him, and receiue him as a wife maried of a virgin.
15.3: With the bread of vnderstanding shall she feed him, and giue him the water of wisedome to drinke.
15.4: Hee shall be stayed vpon her, and shall not be moued, and shall rely vpon her, and shall not be confounded.
15.5: Shee shall exalt him aboue his neighbours, and in the midst of the congregation shall she open his mouth.
15.6: He shall finde ioy, and a crowne of gladnesse, and she shall cause him to inherit an euerlasting name.
15.7: But foolish men shall not attaine vnto her, and sinners shall not see her.
15.8: For she is farre from pride, and men that are liers cannot remember her.
15.9: Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of the Lord:
15.10: For praise shalbe vttered in wisdome, and the Lord wil prosper it.
15.11: Say not thou, It is through the Lord, that I fell away, for thou oughtest not to doe the things that he hateth.
15.12: Say not thou, He hath caused mee to erre, for hee hath no need of the sinfull man.
15.13: The Lord hateth all abomination, and they that feare God loue it not.
15.14: Hee himselfe made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsell,
15.15: If thou wilt, to keepe the Commandements, and to performe acceptable faithfulnesse.
15.16: He hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand vnto whether thou wilt.
15.17: Before man is life and death, and whether him liketh shalbe giuen him.
15.18: For the wisedome of the Lord is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholdeth all things,
15.19: And his eyes are vpon them that feare him, & hee knoweth euery worke of man.
15.20: Hee hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he giuen any man license to sinne.

16.1: Desire not a multitude of vnprofitable children, neither delight in vngodly sonnes.
16.2: Though they multiply, reioyce not in them, except the feare of the Lord be with them.
16.3: Trust not thou in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is iust, is better then a thousand, and better it is to die without children, then to haue them that are vngodly.
16.4: For by one that hath vnderstanding, shall the city be replenished, but the kindred of the wicked, shall speedily become desolate.
16.5: Many such things haue I seene with mine eyes, and mine eare hath heard greater things then these.
16.6: In the congregation of the vngodly, shall a fire be kindled, and in a rebellious nation, wrath is set on fire.
16.7: Hee was not pacified towards the olde giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishnesse.
16.8: Neither spared he the place where Lot soiourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
16.9: Hee pitied not the people of perdition, who were taken away in their sinnes.
16.10: Nor the sixe hundreth thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardnesse of their hearts.
16.11: And if there be one stiffe-necked among the people, it is marueile, if he escape vnpunished; for mercy and wrath are with him, hee is mighty to forgiue, and to powre out displeasure.
16.12: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he iudgeth a man according to his workes.
16.13: The sinner shall not escape with his spoiles, and the patience of the godly shall not be frustrate.
16.14: Make way for euery worke of mercy: for euery man shall finde according to his workes.
16.15: The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that hee should not know him, that his powerfull workes might be knowen to the world.
16.16: His mercy is manifest to euery creature, and hee hath separated his light from the darkenesse with an Adamant.
16.17: Say not thou, I will hide my selfe from the Lord: shall any remember me from aboue? I shall not be remembred among so many people: for what is my soule among such an infinite number of creatures?
16.18: Behold, the heauen, and the heauen of heauens, the deepe and the earth, and all that therein is, shall be mooued when he shall visit.
16.19: The mountaines also, and foundations of the earth shall bee shaken with trembling, when the Lord looketh vpon them.
16.20: No heart can thinke vpon these things worthily: and who is able to conceiue his wayes?
16.21: It is a tempest, which no man can see: for the most part of his workes are hidde.
16.22: Who can declare the workes of his iustice? or who can endure them? for his Couenant is afarre off, and the triall of all things is in the ende.
16.23: He that wanteth vnderstanding, will thinke vpon vaine things: and a foolish man erring, imagineth follies.
16.24: My sonne, hearken vnto mee, and learne knowledge, and marke my words with thy heart.
16.25: I will shewe foorth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly.
16.26: The works of the Lord are done in iudgement from the beginning: and from the time he made them, hee disposed the parts thereof.
16.27: Hee garnished his workes for euer, and in his hand are the chiefe of them vnto all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their workes.
16.28: None of them hindreth another, and they shall neuer disobey his word.
16.29: After this, the Lord looked vpon the earth, and filled it with his blessings.
16.30: With all maner of liuing things hath hee couered the face thereof, and they shall returne into it againe.

17.1: The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it againe.
17.2: He gaue them few dayes, and a short time, and power also ouer the things therein.
17.3: He endued them with strength by themselues, and made them according to his image,
17.4: And put the feare of man vpon all flesh, and gaue him dominion ouer beasts and foules.
17.6: Counsell, and a tongue, and eyes, eares, and a heart, gaue he them to vnderstand.
17.7: Withall, hee filled them with the knowledge of vnderstanding, & shewed them good and euill.
17.8: Hee set his eye vpon their hearts, that he might shew them the greatnesse of his workes.
17.9: He gaue them to glory in his marueilous actes for euer, that they might declare his works with vnderstanding.
17.10: And the elect shall praise his holy Name.
17.11: Beside this he gaue them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
17.12: He made an euerlasting couenant with them, and shewed them his iudgements.
17.13: Their eyes saw the maiestie of his glory, and their eares heard his glorious voyce.
17.14: And he said vnto them, Beware of all vnrighteousnes, and he gaue euery man commandement concerning his neighbour,
17.15: Their wayes are euer before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
17.16: Euery man from his youth is giuen to euil, neither could they make to themselues fleshie hearts for stonie.
17.17: For in the diuision of the nations of the whole earth, he set a ruler ouer euery people, but Israel is the Lords portion.
17.18: Whom being his first borne, hee nourisheth with discipline, and giuing him the light of his loue, doth not forsake him.
17.19: Therefore all their workes are as the Sunne before him, and his eyes are continually vpon their wayes.
17.20: None of their vnrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sinnes are before the Lord:
17.21: But the Lord being gracious, and knowing his workemanship, neither left nor forsooke them, but spared them.
17.22: The almes of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deedes of man, as the apple of the eye, and giue repentance to his sonnes and daughters.
17.23: Afterward he will rise vp and reward them, and render their recompense vpon their heads.
17.24: But vnto them that repent, he granted them returne, and comforted those that faile in patience.
17.25: Returne vnto the Lord, and forsake thy sinnes, make thy prayer before his face, and offend lesse.
17.26: Turne againe to the most High, and turne away from iniquitie: for he will leade thee out of darkenesse into the light of health, and hate thou abomination vehemently.
17.27: Who shall praise the most High in the graue, in stead of them which liue and giue thanks?
17.28: Thankesgiuing perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not: the liuing and sound in heart, shall praise the Lord.
17.29: How great is the louing kindnes of the Lord our God, and his compassion vnto such as turne vnto him in holinesse?
17.30: For all things cannot bee in men, because þe sonne of man is not immortal.
17.31: What is brighter then the Sun? yet the light thereof faileth: and flesh and blood will imagine euill.
17.32: Hee vieweth the power of the height of heauen, and all men are but earth and ashes.

18.1: Hee that liueth for euer, created all things in generall.
18.2: The Lord onely is righteous, and there is none other but he.
18.3: Who gouerneth the world with the palme of his hand, and all things obey his will, for he is the king of all, by his power diuiding holy things among them from prophane.
18.4: To whom hath he giuen power to declare his works? and who shall finde out his noble actes?
18.5: Who shall number the strength of his maiestie? and who shall also tel out his mercies?
18.6: As for the wonderous workes of the Lord, there may nothing bee taken from them, neither may any thing bee put vnto them, neither can the ground of them be found out.
18.7: When a man hath done, then he beginneth, and when hee leaueth off, then he shall be doubtfull.
18.8: What is man, and whereto serueth he? what is his good, & what is his euil?
18.9: The number of a mans dayes at the most are an hundred yeeres.
18.10: As a drop of water vnto the Sea, and a grauell stone in comparison of the sand, so are a thousand yeeres to the dayes of eternitie.
18.11: Therfore is God patient with them, & powreth forth his mercy vpon them.
18.12: He saw and perceiued their end to be euill, therefore he multiplied his compassion.
18.13: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour, but the mercy of the Lord is vpon all flesh: he reprooueth and nurtureth, and teacheth, & bringeth againe as a shepheard his flocke.
18.14: He hath mercy on them that receiue discipline, and that diligently seeke after his iudgements.
18.15: My sonne, blemish not thy good deeds, neither vse vncomfortable words when thou giuest any thing.
18.16: Shall not the deaw asswage the heate? so is a word better then a gift.
18.17: Loe is not a word better then a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
18.18: A foole will vpbraide churlishly, and a gift of the enuious consumeth the eyes.
18.19: Learne before thou speake, and vse phisicke, or euer thou be sicke.
18.20: Before iudgement examine thy selfe, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.
18.21: Humble thy selfe before thou be sicke, and in the time of sinnes shew repentance.
18.22: Let nothing hinder thee to pay thy vowe in due time, and deferre not vntill death to be iustified.
18.23: Before thou prayest, prepare thy selfe, and be not as one that tempteth the Lord.
18.24: Thinke vpon the wrath that shall be at the end; and the time of vengeance when he shall turne away his face.
18.25: When thou hast enough remember the time of hunger, and when thou art rich thinke vpon pouerty and need.
18.26: From the morning vntill the euening the time is changed, and all things are soone done before the Lord.
18.27: A wise man will feare in euery thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a foole will not obserue time.
18.28: Euery man of vnderstanding knoweth wisedome, and wil giue praise vnto him that found her.
18.29: They that were of vnderstanding in sayings, became also wise themselues, and powred forth exquisite parables.
18.30: Goe not after thy lustes, but refraine thy selfe from thine appetites.
18.31: If thou giuest thy soule the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughing stocke to thine enemies, that maligne thee.
18.32: Take not pleasure in much good cheere, neither be tyed to the expence thereof.
18.33: Be not made a begger by banquetting vpon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse, for thou shalt lie in waite for thy owne life: and be talked on.

19.1: A labouring man that is giuen to drunkennesse shal not be rich, and hee that contemneth small things shall fall by little & little.
19.2: Wine and women will make men of vnderstanding to fall away, and he that cleaueth to harlots will become impudent.
19.3: Mothes and wormes shall haue him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.
19.4: He that is hasty to giue credit is light minded, and he that sinneth shall offend against his owne soule.
19.5: Who so taketh pleasure in wickednesse shall be condemned, but he that resisteth pleasures, crowneth his life.
19.6: He that can rule his tongue shall liue without strife, and he that hateth babbling, shall haue lesse euill.
19.7: Rehearse not vnto another that which is told vnto thee, and thou shalt fare neuer the worse.
19.8: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other mens liues, and if thou canst without offence reueale them not.
19.9: For he heard and obserued thee, and when time commeth he will hate thee.
19.10: If thou hast heard a word, let it die with thee, and be bold it will not burst thee.
19.11: A foole trauaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.
19.12: As an arrowe that sticketh in a mans thigh, so is a word within a fooles belly.
19.13: Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it, and if he haue that he doe it no more.
19.14: Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it, and if he haue, that he speake it not againe.
19.15: Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, & beleeue not euery tale.
19.16: There is one that slippeth in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?
19.17: Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him, and not being angry giue place to the Law of the most high.
19.18: The feare of the Lord is the first step to be accepted and wisedome obtaineth his loue.
19.19: The knowledge of the Commandements of the Lord, is the doctrine of life, and they that do things that please him, shall receiue the fruit of the tree of immortalitie.
19.20: The feare of the Lord is all wisedome, and in all wisedome is the performance of the Law, and the knowledge of his omnipotencie.
19.21: If a seruant say to his master, I will not doe as it pleaseth thee, though afterward hee doe it, hee angereth him that nourisheth him.
19.22: The knowledge of wickednes is not wisedome, neither at any time the counsell of sinners, prudence.
19.23: There is a wickednesse, and the same an abomination, and there is a foole wanting in wisedome.
19.24: He that hath smal vnderstanding and feareth God, is better then one that hath much wisedome, and transgresseth the Law of the most High.
19.25: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is vniust, and there is one that turneth aside to make iudgement appeare: and there is a wise man that iustifieth in iudgement.
19.26: There is a wicked man that hangeth downe his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
19.27: Casting downe his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not knowen, he will do thee a mischiefe before thou be aware.
19.28: And if for want of power hee be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunitie he wil doe euil.
19.29: A man may bee knowen by his looke, and one that hath vnderstanding, by his countenance, when thou meetest him.
19.30: A mans attire, and excessiue laughter, and gate, shew what he is.

20.1: There is a reproofe that is not comely: againe some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.
20.2: It is much better to reprooue, then to be angry secretly, and he that confesseth his fault, shall be preserued from hurt.
20.3: How good is it when thou art reproued, to shew repentance? for so shalt thou escape wilfull sinne.
20.4: As is the lust of an Eunuch to defloure a virgine; so is he that executeth iudgement with violence.
20.5: There is one that keepeth silence and is found wise: and another by much babling becommeth hatefull.
20.6: Some man holdeth his tongue, because hee hath not to answere, and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.
20.7: A wise man wil hold his tongue till he see opportunitie: but a babler and a foole will regard no time.
20.8: He that vseth many words shalbe abhorred; and hee that taketh to himselfe authoritie therein, shalbe hated.
20.9: There is a sinner that hath good successe in euill things; and there is a gaine that turneth to losse.
20.10: There is a gift that shall not profit thee; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.
20.11: There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth vp his head from a low estate.
20.12: There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it seuen fold.
20.13: A wise man by his words maketh himselfe beloued: but the graces of fooles shalbe powred out.
20.14: The gift of a foole shall doe thee no good when thou hast it; neither yet of the enuious for his necessitie: for hee looketh to receiue many things for one.
20.15: Hee giueth little and vpbraideth much; hee openeth his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he aske it againe: such an one is to be hated of God and man.
20.16: The foole saith, I haue no friends, I haue no thanke for all my good deeds: and they that eate my bread speake euill of me.
20.17: How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorne? for hee knoweth not aright what it is to haue; and it is all one vnto him, as if he had it not.
20.18: To slip vpon a pauement, is better then to slip with the tongue: so, the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
20.19: An vnseasonable tale will alwayes be in the mouth of the vnwise.
20.20: A wise sentence shall be reiected when it commeth out of a fools mouth: for he will not speake it in due season.
20.21: There is that is hindred from sinning through want: and when hee taketh rest, he shall not be troubled.
20.22: There is that destroyeth his owne soule through bashfulnesse, and by accepting of persons ouerthroweth himselfe.
20.23: There is that for bashfulnes promiseth to his friend, and maketh him his enemy for nothing.
20.24: A lie is a foule blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the vntaught.
20.25: A thiefe is better then a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall haue destruction to heritage.
20.26: The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is euer with him.
20.27: A wise man shall promote himselfe to honour with his words: and hee that hath vnderstanding, will please great men.
20.28: He that tilleth his land, shall increase his heape: and he that pleaseth great men, shal get pardon for iniquity.
20.29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stoppe vp his mouth that he cannot reprooue.
20.30: Wisedome that is hidde, and treasure that is hoarded vp, what profit is in them both?
20.31: Better is he that hideth his folly, then a man that hideth his wisedome.
20.32: Necessary patience in seeking the Lord, is better then he that leadeth his life without a guide.

21.1: My sonne, hast thou sinned? doe so no more, but aske pardon for thy former sinnes.
21.2: Flee from sinne as from the face of a Serpent: for if thou commest too neere it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof, are as the teeth of a lyon, slaying the soules of men.
21.3: All iniquitie is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.
21.4: To terrifie and doe wrong, will waste riches: thus the house of proude men shalbe made desolate.
21.5: A prayer out of a poore mans mouth reacheth to the eares of God, and his iudgement commeth speedily.
21.6: He that hateth to be reprooued, is in the way of sinners: but hee that feareth the Lord, will repent from his heart.
21.7: An eloquent man is knowen farre and neere, but a man of vnderstanding knoweth when he slippeth.
21.8: He that buildeth his house with other mens money, is like one that gathereth himselfe stones for the tombe of his buriall.
21.9: The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.
21.10: The way of sinners is made plaine with stones, but at the ende thereof is the pit of hell.
21.11: Hee that keepeth the Law of the Lord, getteth the vnderstanding thereof: and the perfection of the feare of the Lord, is wisedome.
21.12: He that is not wise, will not be taught: but there is a wisedome which multiplieth bitternesse.
21.13: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsell is like a pure fountaine of life.
21.14: The inner parts of a foole, are like a broken vessell, and he will holde no knowledge as long as he liueth.
21.15: If a skilfull man heare a wise word, hee will commend it, and adde vnto it: but assoone as one of no vnderstanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behinde his backe.
21.16: The talking of a foole is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
21.17: They inquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
21.18: As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisedome to a foole: and the knowledge of the vnwise, is as talke without sense.
21.19: Doctrine vnto fooles, is as fetters on the feete, and like manacles on the right hand.
21.20: A foole lifteth vp his voyce with laughter, but a wise man doeth scarce smile a litle.
21.21: Learning is vnto a wise man, as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet vpon his right arme.
21.22: A foolish mans foote is soone in his house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.
21.23: A foole will peepe in at the doore into the house, but he that is well nurtured, will stand without.
21.24: It is the rudenesse of a man to hearken at the doore: but a wise man will be grieued with the disgrace.
21.25: The lips of talkers will bee telling such things as pertaine not vnto them: but the words of such as haue vnderstanding, are weighed in the ballance.
21.26: The heart of fooles is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
21.27: When the vngodly curseth Satan, he curseth his owne soule.
21.28: A whisperer defileth his owne soule, and is hated wheresoeuer hee dwelleth.

22.1: A slouthful man is compared to a filthy stone, and euery one will hisse him out to his disgrace.
22.2: A slouthfull man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: euery man that takes it vp, will shake his hand.
22.3: An euill nurtured sonne is the dishonour of his father that begate him: and a daughter is borne to his losse.
22.4: A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but shee that liueth dishonestly, is her fathers heauinesse.
22.5: Shee that is bold, dishonoureth both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her.
22.6: A tale out of season musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisedome are neuer out of time.
22.7: Who so teacheth a foole, is as one that gleweth a potsheard together, and as hee that waketh one from a sound sleepe.
22.8: Hee that telleth a tale to a foole, speaketh to one in a slumber: when hee hath told his tale, he will say, What is the matter?
22.9: If children liue honestly, and haue wherwithall, they shall couer the basenesse of their parents.
22.10: But children being haughtie through disdaine, and want of nurture, doe staine the nobilitie of their kinred.
22.11: Weepe for the dead, for hee hath lost the light: and weepe for the foole, for he wanteth vnderstanding: make litle weeping for the dead, for hee is at rest: but the life of the foole is worse then death.
22.12: Seuen dayes doe men mourne for him that is dead; but for a foole, and an vngodly man, all the dayes of his life.
22.13: Talke not much with a foole, and goe not to him that hath no vnderstanding, beware of him lest thou haue trouble, and thou shalt neuer be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and thou shalt find rest, and neuer bee disquieted with madnesse.
22.14: What is heauier then lead? and what is the name thereof, but a foole?
22.15: Sand, and salt, and a masse of yron is easier to beare then a man without vnderstanding.
22.16: As timber girt and bound together in a building, cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by aduised counsel, shal feare at no time.
22.17: A heart setled vpon a thought of vnderstanding, is as a faire plaistering on the wall of a gallerie.
22.18: Pales set on an high place will neuer stand against the wind: so a feareful heart in the imagination of a foole, can not stand against any feare.
22.19: He that pricketh the eye, wil make teares to fall: and he that pricketh the heart, maketh it to shewe her knowledge.
22.20: Who so casteth a stone at the birds, frayeth them away, and he that vpbraideth his friend, breaketh friendship.
22.21: Though thou drewest a sword at thy friend, yet despaire not, for there way be a returning (to fauour.)
22.22: If thou hast opened thy mouth against thy friend, feare not, for there may be a reconciliation: except for vpbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound, for, for these things euery friend will depart.
22.23: Be faithfull to thy neighbour in his pouertie, that thou mayest reioyce in his prosperitie: abide stedfast vnto him in the time of his trouble, that thou mayest bee heire with him in his heritage: for a meane estate is not alwayes to be contemned, nor the rich that is foolish, to be had in admiration.
22.24: As the vapour and smoke of a furnace goeth before the fire: so reuiling before blood.
22.25: I will not be ashamed to defend a friend: neither will I hide my selfe from him.
22.26: And if any euill happen vnto me by him, euery one that heareth it will beware of him.
22.27: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seale of wisedome vpon my lippes, that I fall not suddenly by them, & that my tongue destroy me not?

23.1: O Lord, father and gouernour of all my whole life, leaue me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.
23.2: Who will set scourges ouer my thoughts, and the discipline of wisedome ouer mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances and it passe not by my sinnes:
23.3: Least mine ignorances increase, and my sinnes abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine aduersaries, and mine enemie reioyce ouer mee, whose hope is farre from thy mercy.
23.4: O Lord, father and God of my life, giue me not a proud looke, but turne away from thy seruants alwaies a haughty minde:
23.5: Turne away from mee vaine hopes, and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him vp that is desirous alwaies to serue thee.
23.6: Let not the greedinesse of the belly, nor lust of the flesh take hold of me, and giue not ouer me thy seruant into an impudent minde.
23.7: Heare, O yee children, the discipline of the mouth: He that keepeth it, shall neuer be taken in his lippes.
23.8: The sinner shall be left in his foolishnesse: both the euill speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.
23.9: Accustome not thy mouth to swearing: neither vse thy selfe to the naming of the holy one.
23.10: For as a seruant that is continually beaten, shall not be without a blew marke: so hee that sweareth and nameth God continually, shal not be faultlesse.
23.11: A man that vseth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall neuer depart from his house: If he shall offend, his sinne shall be vpon him: and if he acknowledge not his sinne, hee maketh a double offence, and if he sweare in vaine, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.
23.12: There is a word that is clothed about with death: God graunt that it be not found in the heritage of Iacob, for all such things shall be farre from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sinnes.
23.13: Use not thy mouth to vntemperate swearing, for therein is the word of sinne.
23.14: Remember thy father and thy mother, when thou sittest among great men. Be not forgetfull before them, and so thou by thy custome become a foole, and wish that thou hadst not beene borne, and curse the day of thy natiuitie.
23.15: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will neuer be reformed all the daies of his life.
23.16: Two sorts of men multiply sinne, and the third will bring wrath: a hot minde is as a burning fire, it will neuer be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicatour in the body of his flesh, will neuer cease till he hath kindled a fire.
23.17: All bread is sweete to a whoremonger, he will not leaue off till he die.
23.18: A man that breaketh wedlocke, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darknesse: the walles couer me; & no body seeth me, what neede I to feare? The most high wil not remember my sinnes:
23.19: Such a man only feareth the eies of men, and knoweth not that the eies of the Lord are tenne thousand times brighter then the Sunne, beholding all the waies of men, and considering the most secret parts.
23.20: He knew all things ere euer they were created, so also after they were perfited, he looked vpon them all:
23.21: This man shall bee punished in the streets of the citie, and where he suspecteth not, he shall be taken.
23.22: Thus shall it goe also with the wife, that leaueth her husband, and bringeth in an heire by another:
23.23: For first she hath disobeyed the Law of the most High: and secondly, she hath trespassed against her owne husband, and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.
23.24: Shee shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shalbe made of her children.
23.25: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring foorth no fruit.
23.26: She shall leaue her memorie to be cursed, and her reproch shall not be blotted out.
23.27: And they that remaine, shall know that there is nothing better then the feare of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter then to take heed vnto the Commandement of the Lord.
23.28: It is great glory to follow the Lord, & to be receiued of him is long life.

24.1: Wisedome shall praise her selfe, and shall glory in the midst of her people.
24.2: In the Congregation of the most high, shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.
24.3: I came out of the mouth of the most High, and couered the earth as a cloud.
24.4: I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
24.5: I alone compassed the circuit of heauen, and walked in the bottome of the deepe.
24.6: In the waues of the sea, and in all the earth, and in euery people, and nation, I got a possession.
24.7: With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?
24.8: So the creatour of all things gaue mee a commandement, and hee that made me, caused my tabernacle to rest: and said, Let thy dwelling be in Iacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.
24.9: Hee created mee from the beginning before the world, and I shall neuer faile.
24.10: In the holy Tabernacle I serued before him: and so was I established in Sion.
24.11: Likewise in the beloued citie he gaue mee rest, and in Ierusalem was my power.
24.12: And I tooke roote in an honourable people, euen in the portion of the Lords inheritance.
24.13: I was exalted like a Cedar in Libanus, and as a Cypresse tree vpon the mountaines of Hermon.
24.14: I was exalted like a palme tree in Engaddi, and as a rose-plant in Iericho, as a faire oliue tree in a pleasant fielde, and grew vp as a planetree by the water.
24.15: I gaue a sweete smell like cinamon, and aspalathus, and I yeelded a pleasant odour like the best mirrhe, as Galbanum and Onix, and sweet Storax, and as the sume of franckincense in the Tabernacle.
24.16: As the Turpentine tree, I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.
24.17: As the Uine brought I foorth pleasant sauour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
24.18: I am the mother of faire loue, and feare, and knowledge, and holy hope, I therefore being eternall, am giuen to all my children which are named of him.
24.19: Come vnto me all ye that be desirous of mee, and fill your selues with my fruits.
24.20: For my memorial is sweeter then hony, and mine inheritance then the hony combe.
24.21: They that eate mee shall yet be hungry, and they that drinke me shall yet be thirstie.
24.22: He that obeyeth me, shall neuer be confounded, and they that worke by me, shall not doe amisse.
24.23: All these things are the booke of the Couenant of the most high God, euen the Law which Moses commanded for an heritage vnto the Congregations of Iacob.
24.24: Faint not to bee strong in the Lord; that he may confirme you, cleaue vnto him: for the Lord Almightie is God alone, and besides him there is no other Sauiour.
24.25: He filleth all things with his wisdome, as Physon, and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
24.26: He maketh the vnderstanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Iorden in the time of the haruest.
24.27: He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appeare as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.
24.28: The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last finde her out.
24.29: For her thoughts are more then the Sea, and her counsels profounder then the great deepe.
24.30: I also came out as a brooke from a riuer, and as a conduit into a garden.
24.31: I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bedde: and loe, my brooke became a riuer, and my riuer became a sea.
24.32: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afarre off.
24.33: I will yet powre out doctrine as prophecie, and leaue it to all ages for euer.
24.34: Behold that I haue not laboured for my selfe onely, but for all them that seeke wisedome.

25.1: In three things I was beautified, and stoode vp beautiful, both before God and men: the vnitie of brethren, the loue of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.
25.2: Three sorts of men my soule hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poore man that is proud, a rich man that is a lyar, and an olde adulterer that doteth.
25.3: If thou hast gathered nothing in thy youth, how canst thou finde any thing in thine age?
25.4: Oh how comely a thing is iudgement for gray haires, and for ancient men to know counsell?
25.5: Oh how comely is the wisedome of olde men, and vnderstanding and counsell to men of honour?
25.6: Much experience is the crowne of olde men, and the feare of God is their glory.
25.7: There be nine things which I haue iudged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will vtter with my tongue: a man that hath ioy of his children, and he that liueth to see the fall of his enemie.
25.8: Well is him that dwelleth with a wife of vnderstanding, and that hath not slipped with his tongue, and that hath not serued a man more vnworthy then himselfe.
25.9: Well is him that hath found prudence, and he that speaketh in the eares of him that will heare.
25.10: Oh how great is he that findeth wisedome! yet is there none aboue him that feareth the Lord.
25.11: But the loue of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?
25.12: The feare of the Lord is the beginning of his loue: and faith is the beginning of cleauing vnto him.
25.13: any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickednesse, but the wickednesse of a woman.
25.14: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any reuenge, but the reuenge of enemies.
25.15: There is no head aboue the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath aboue the wrath of an enemie.
25.16: I had rather dwell with a lyon and a dragon, then to keepe house with a wicked woman.
25.17: The wickednesse of a woman changeth her face, and darkeneth her countenance like sackecloth.
25.18: Her husband shall sit among his neighbours: and when hee heareth it, shall sigh bitterly.
25.19: All wickednesse is but little to the wickednesse of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall vpon her.
25.20: As the climbing vp a sandie way is to the feete of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
25.21: Stumble not at the beautie of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.
25.22: A woman, if shee maintaine her husband, is full of anger, impudencie, and much reproch.
25.23: A wicked woman abateth the courage, maketh a heauie countenance, and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distresse maketh weake hands, and feeble knees.
25.24: Of the woman came the beginning of sinne, & through her wee all die.
25.25: Giue the water no passage: neither a wicked woman libertie to gad abroad.
25.26: If she goe not as thou wouldest haue her, cut her off from thy flesh, and giue her a bill of diuorce, and let her goe.

26.1: Blessed is the man that hath a vertuous wife, for the number of his dayes shall be double.
26.2: A vertuous woman reioyceth her husband, and he shall fulfill the yeeres of his life in peace.
26.3: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be giuen in the portion of them that feare the Lord.
26.4: Whether a man be rich or poore, if he haue a good heart towards the Lord, he shall at all times reioyce with a cheerefull countenance.
26.5: There bee three things that mine heart feareth: and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a citie, the gathering together of an vnruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse then death.
26.6: But a griefe of heart and sorrow, is a woman that is ielous ouer another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth withall.
26.7: An euil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that hath hold of her, is as though he held a scorpion.
26.8: A drunken woman and a gadder abroad, causeth great anger, and shee will not couer her owne shame.
26.9: The whordome of a woman may be knowen in her haughtie lookes, and eye lids.
26.10: If thy daughter be shamelesse, keepe her in straitly: lest she abuse her selfe through ouermuch libertie.
26.11: Watch ouer an impudent eye: and marueile not, if shee trespasse against thee.
26.12: Shee will open her mouth as a thirstie traueiler, when he hath found a fountaine: and drinke of euery water neere her: by euery hedge will she sit downe, and open her quiuer against euery arrow.
26.13: The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fat his bones.
26.14: A silent and louing woman is a gift of the Lord, and there is nothing so much worth, as a mind well instructed.
26.15: A shamefast and faithfull woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.
26.16: As the Sunne when it ariseth in the high heauen: so is the beautie of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
26.17: As the cleare light is vpon the holy candlesticke: so is the beautie of the face in ripe age.
26.18: As the golden pillars are vpon the sockets of siluer: so are the faire feete with a constant heart.
26.19: My sonne, keepe the flowre of thine age sound: and giue not thy strength to strangers.
26.20: When thou hast gotten a fruitfull possession through all the field: sowe it with thine owne seede, trusting in the goodnesse of thy stocke.
26.21: So thy race which thou leauest shalbe magnified, hauing the confidence of their good descent.
26.22: An harlot shall bee accounted as spittle: but a maried woman is a towre against death to her husband.
26.23: A wicked woman is giuen as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is giuen to him that feareth the Lord.
26.24: A dishonest woman contemneth shame, but an honest woman will reuerence her husband.
26.25: A shamelesse woman shalbe counted as a dog: but she that is shamefast will feare the Lord.
26.26: A woman that honoureth her husband, shall bee iudged wise of all: but she that dishonoureth him in her pride, shall be counted vngodly of all.
26.27: A loude crying woman, and a scolde, shall be sought out to driue away the enemies.
26.28: There be two things that grieue my heart: and the third maketh me angry: a man of warre that suffereth pouerty, and men of vnderstanding that are not set by: and one that returneth from righteousnesse to sinne: the Lord prepareth such a one for the sword.
26.29: A merchant shall hardly keepe himselfe from doing wrong: and an huckster shall not be freed from sinne.

27.1: Many haue sinned for a smal matter: & he that seeketh for abundance will turne his eies away.
27.2: As a naile sticketh fast betweene the ioynings of the stones: so doth sinne sticke close betweene buying and selling.
27.3: Unlesse a man hold himselfe diligently in the feare of the Lord, his house shall soone be ouerthrowen.
27.4: As when one sifteth with a sieue, the refuse remaineth, so the filth of man in his talke.
27.5: The furnace prooueth the potters vessell: so the triall of man is in his reasoning.
27.6: The fruite declareth if the tree haue beene dressed: so is the vtterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
27.7: Praise no man before thou hearest him speake, for this is the triall of men.
27.8: If thou followest righteousnesse, thou shalt obtaine her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.
27.9: The birds will resort vnto their like, so will truth returne vnto them that practise in her.
27.10: As the Lyon lieth in waite for the pray: so sinne for them that worke iniquity.
27.11: The discourse of a godly man is alwaies with wisedome: but a foole changeth as the Moone.
27.12: If thou be among the vndiscreet, obserue the time: but be continually among men of vnderstanding.
27.13: The discourse of fooles is irksome, and their sport is in the wantonnesse of sinne.
27.14: The talke of him that sweareth much, maketh the haire stand vpright: and their braules make one stop his eares.
27.15: The strife of the proud is blood-shedding, and their reuilings are grieuous to the eare.
27.16: Who so discouereth secrets, looseth his credit: and shall neuer find friend to his minde.
27.17: Loue thy friend, and be faithfull vnto him: but if thou bewrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.
27.18: For as a man hath destroyed his enemie: so hast thou lost the loue of thy neighbour.
27.19: As one that letteth a bird goe out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour goe; and shalt not get him againe.
27.20: Follow after him no more, for he is too far off, he is as a roe escaped out of the snare.
27.21: As for a wound it may be bound vp, and after reuiling there may be reconcilement: but he that bewrayeth secrets is without hope.
27.22: He that winketh with the eies worketh euil, and he that knoweth him will depart from him.
27.23: When thou art present he will speake sweetly, and will admire thy words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander thy sayings.
27.24: I haue hated many things, but nothing like him, for the Lord will hate him.
27.25: Who so casteth a stone on high, casteth it on his owne head, and a deceitfull stroke shall make wounds.
27.26: Who so diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.
27.27: He that worketh mischiefe, it shall fall vpon him, and he shall not know whence it commeth.
27.28: Mockery and reproach are from the proud: but vengeance as a Lyon shall lie in waite for them.
27.29: They that reioyce at the fall of the righteous shalbe taken in the snare, and anguish shall consume them before they die.
27.30: Malice and wrath, euen these are abhominations, and the sinfull man shall haue them both.

28.1: He that reuengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keepe his sinnes (in remembrance.)
28.2: Forgiue thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done vnto thee, so shall thy sinnes also be forgiuen when thou prayest.
28.3: One man beareth hatred against another, and doeth he seeke pardon from the Lord?
28.4: Hee sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himselfe: and doeth hee aske forgiuenesse of his owne sinnes?
28.5: If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sinnes?
28.6: Remember thy end, and let enimitie cease, corruption and death, and abide in the Commandements.
28.7: Remember the Commaundements, & beare no malice to thy neighbour: the Couenant of the highest, and winke at ignorance.
28.8: Abstaine from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sinnes: for a furious man will kindle strife.
28.9: A sinfull man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace.
28.10: As the matter of the fire is, so it burneth: and as a mans strength is, so is his wrath, and according to his riches his anger riseth, and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed.
28.11: An hastie contention kindleth a fire, and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood.
28.12: If thou blow the sparke, it shall burne: if thou spit vpon it, it shall bee quenched, and both these come out of thy mouth.
28.13: Curse the whisperer, and double tongued: for such haue destroyed many that were at peace.
28.14: A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driuen them from nation to nation, strong cities hath it pulled down, and ouerthrowen the houses of great men.
28.15: A backbiting tongue hath cast out vertuous women, and depriued them of their labours.
28.16: Who so hearkeneth vnto it, shall neuer finde rest, and neuer dwel quietly.
28.17: The stroke of the whip maketh markes in the flesh, but the stroke of the tongue breaketh the bones.
28.18: Many haue fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as haue fallen by the tongue.
28.19: Well is hee that is defended from it, and hath not passed through the venime thereof: who hath not drawen the yoke thereof, nor hath bene bound in her bands.
28.20: For the yoke thereof is a yoke of yron, and the bands thereof are bandes of brasse.
28.21: The death therof is an euil death, the graue were better then it.
28.22: It shall not haue rule ouer them that feare God, neither shall they be burnt with the flame thereof.
28.23: Such as forsake the Lord shall fall into it, and it shall burne in them, and not be quenched, it shalbe sent vpon them as a Lion, and deuoure them as a Leopard.
28.24: Looke that thou hedge thy possession about with thornes, and binde vp thy siluer and gold:
28.25: And weigh thy words in a ballance, and make a doore and barre for thy mouth.
28.26: Beware thou slide not by it, lest thou fall before him that lieth in wait.

29.1: Hee that is mercifull, will lende vnto his neighbour, and hee that strengthneth his hande, keepeth the Commandements.
29.2: Lend to thy neighbour in time of his need, and pay thou thy neighbour againe in due season.
29.3: Keepe thy word & deale faithfully with him, and thou shalt alwaies finde the thing that is necessary for thee.
29.4: Many when a thing was lent them, reckoned it to be found, and put them to trouble that helped them.
29.5: Till he hath receiued, he will kisse a mans hand: and for his neighbours money he will speake submissely: but when he should repay, he will prolong the time, and returne words of griefe, and complaine of the time.
29.6: If he preuaile, he shall hardly receiue the halfe, and he will count as if he had found it: if not; he hath depriued him of his money, and he hath gotten him an enemy without cause: he payeth him with cursings, and raylings: and for honour he will pay him disgrace.
29.7: Many therefore haue refused to lend for other mens ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded.
29.8: Yet haue thou patience with a man in poore estate, and delay not to shew him mercy.
29.9: Helpe the poore for the commandements sake, and turne him not away because of his pouertie.
29.10: Lose thy money for thy brother and thy friend, and let it not rust vnder a stone to be lost.
29.11: Lay vp thy treasure according to the commandements of the most high, and it shall bring thee more profite then golde.
29.12: Shut vp almes in thy storehouses: and it shall deliuer thee from all affliction.
29.13: It shal fight for thee against thine enemies, better then a mightie shield and strong speare.
29.14: An honest man is suretie for his neighbour: but hee that is impudent, will forsake him.
29.15: Forget not the friendship of thy suretie: for hee hath giuen his life for thee.
29.16: A sinner will ouerthrow the good estate of his suretie:
29.17: And he that is of an vnthankfull minde, will leaue him in that deliuered him.
29.18: Suretiship hath vndone many of good estate, and shaked them as a waue of the Sea: mightie men hath it driuen from their houses, so that they wandred among strange nations.
29.19: A wicked man transgressing the commandements of the Lord, shall fall into suretiship: and hee that vndertaketh and followeth other mens businesse for gaine, shall fall into suits.
29.20: Helpe thy neighbour according to thy power, and beware that thou thy selfe fall not into the same.
29.21: The chiefe thing for life is water and bread, and clothing, and an house to couer shame.
29.22: Better is the life of a poore man in a meane cottage, then delicate fare in another mans house.
29.23: Be it little or much, holde thee contented, that thou heare not the reproch of thy house.
29.24: For it is a miserable life to goe from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.
29.25: Thou shalt entertaine and feast, and haue no thankes: moreouer, thou shalt heare bitter words.
29.26: Come thou stranger, and furnish a table, and feede me of that thou hast ready.
29.27: Giue place thou stranger to an honourable man, my brother commeth to be lodged, and I haue neede of mine house.
29.28: These things are grieuous to a man of vnderstanding: the vpbraiding of house-roome, and reproching of the lender.

30.1: Hee that loueth his sonne, causeth him oft to feele the rodde, that hee may haue ioy of him in the end.
30.2: He that chastiseth his sonne, shall haue ioy in him, and shall reioyce of him among his acquaintance.
30.3: He that teacheth his sonne, grieueth the enemie: and before his friends he shall reioyce of him.
30.4: Though his father die, yet he is as though hee were not dead: for hee hath left one behinde him that is like himselfe.
30.5: While he liued, he saw and reioyced in him: and when he died hee was not sorrowfull.
30.6: He left behinde him an auenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindnesse to his friends.
30.7: He that maketh too much of his sonne, shall binde vp his wounds, and his bowels wil be troubled at euery cry.
30.8: An horse not broken becommeth headstrong: and a childe left to himselfe will be wilfull.
30.9: Cocker thy childe, and hee shall make thee afraid: play with him, and he will bring thee to heauinesse.
30.10: Laugh not with him, lest thou haue sorrow with him, and lest thou gnash thy teeth in the end.
30.11: Giue him no liberty in his youth, and winke not at his follies.
30.12: Bow downe his necke while hee is young, and beate him on the sides while he is a childe, lest hee waxe stubborne, and be disobedient vnto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.
30.13: Chastise thy sonne, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behauiour be an offence vnto thee.
30.14: Better is the poore being sound and strong of constitution, then a rich man that is afflicted in his body.
30.15: Health and good state of body are aboue all gold, and a strong body aboue infinite wealth.
30.16: There is no riches aboue a sound body, and no ioy aboue the ioy of the heart.
30.17: Death is better then a bitter life, or continuall sickenesse.
30.18: Delicates powred vpon a mouth shut vp, are as messes of meat set vpon a graue.
30.19: What good doth the offering vnto an idole? for neither can it eat nor smell: so is he that is persecuted of the Lord.
30.20: Hee seeth with his eyes and groneth, as an Eunuch that embraceth a virgine, and sigheth.
30.21: Giue not ouer thy mind to heauinesse, and afflict not thy selfe in thine owne counsell.
30.22: The gladnesse of the heart is the life of man, and the ioyfulnes of a man prolongeth his dayes.
30.23: Loue thine owne soule, and comfort thy heart, remoue sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein.
30.24: Enuie and wrath shorten the life, and carefulnesse bringeth age before the time.
30.25: A cherefull and good heart will haue a care of his meat and diet.

31.1: Watching for riches, consumeth the flesh, and the care therof driueth away sleepe.
31.2: Watching care will not let a man slumber, as a sore disease breaketh sleepe.
31.3: The rich hath great labour in gathering riches together, and when he resteth, he is filled with his delicates.
31.4: The poore laboureth in his poore estate, and when he leaueth off, hee is still needie.
31.5: He that loueth gold shall not bee iustified, and he that followeth corruption, shall haue enough thereof.
31.6: Gold hath bin the ruine of many, and their destruction was present.
31.7: It is a stumbling block vnto them that sacrifice vnto it, and euery foole shall be taken therewith.
31.8: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and hath not gone after gold:
31.9: Who is he? and we will call him blessed: for wonderfull things hath hee done among his people.
31.10: Who hath bene tried thereby, and found perfit? then let him glory. Who might offend and hath not offended, or done euill, and hath not done it?
31.11: His goods shall be established, and the congregatiō shall declare his almes.
31.12: If thou sit at a bountifull table, bee not greedy vpon it, and say not, There is much meate on it.
31.13: Remember that a wicked eye is an euill thing: and what is created more wicked then an eye? therefore it weepeth vpon euery occasion.
