31.14: Stretch not thine hand whithersoeuer it looketh, and thrust it not with him into the dish.
31.15: Iudge of thy neighbour by thy selfe: and be discreet in euery point.
31.16: Eate as it becommeth a man those things which are set before thee: and deuoure not, lest thou be hated.
31.17: Leaue off first for maners sake, and be not vnsatiable, lest thou offend.
31.18: When thou sittest among many, reach not thine hand out first of all.
31.19: A very litle is sufficient for a man well nurtured, and he fetcheth not his wind short vpon his bed.
31.20: Sound sleepe commeth of moderate eating: he riseth early, and his wits are with him, but the paine of watching and choller, and pangs of the bellie are with an vnsatiable man.
31.21: And if thou hast bin forced to eate, arise, goe forth, vomit, and thou shalt haue rest.
31.22: My sonne, heare me, and despise me not, and at the last thou shalt finde as I told thee: in all thy workes bee quicke, so shall there no sickenesse come vnto thee.
31.23: Who so is liberall of his meat, men shall speake well of him, and the report of his good housekeeping will be beleeued.
31.24: But against him that is a niggard of his meate, the whole citie shall murmure; and the testimonies of his niggardnesse shall not be doubted of.
31.25: Shew not thy valiantnesse in wine, for wine hath destroyed many.
31.26: The furnace prooueth the edge by dipping: so doth wine the hearts of the proud by drunkennesse.
31.27: Wine is as good as life to a man if it be drunke moderatly: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.
31.28: Wine measurably drunke, and in season, bringeth gladnesse of the heart and cheerefulnesse of the minde.
31.29: But wine drunken with excesse, maketh bitternesse of the minde, with brawling and quarreling.
31.30: Drunkennesse increaseth the rage of a foole till he offend, it diminisheth strength, and maketh wounds.
31.31: Rebuke not thy neighbour at the wine, and despise him not in his mirth: giue him no despitefull words, and presse not vpon him with vrging him (to drinke.)

32.1: If thou be made the master (of the feast) lift not thy selfe vp, but bee among them as one of the rest, take diligent care for them, and so sit downe.
32.2: And when thou hast done all thy office, take thy place that thou mayest be merry with them, and receiue a crowne for thy well ordering of the feast.
32.3: Speake thou that art the elder, for it becometh thee, but with sound iudgement, and hinder not musicke.
32.4: Powre not out words where there is a musitian, and shew not forth wisedome out of time.
32.5: A consort of musicke in a banket of wine, is as a signet of Carbuncle set in gold.
32.6: As a signet of an Emeraud set in a worke of gold, so is the melodie of musicke with pleasant wine.
32.7: Speake yong man, if there be need of thee: and yet scarsely when thou art twise asked:
32.8: Let thy speach be short, comprehending much in few words, be as one that knoweth, and yet holdeth his tongue.
32.9: If thou be among great men, make not thy selfe equall with them, and when ancient men are in place, vse not many words.
32.10: Before the thunder goeth lightening: and before a shamefast man shall goe fauour.
32.11: Rise vp betimes, and be not the last: but get thee home without delay.
32.12: There take thy pastime, & do what thou wilt: but sinne not by proud speach
32.13: And for these things blesse him that made thee, and hath replenished thee with his good things.
32.14: Who so feareth the Lord, will receiue his discipline, and they that seeke him early, shall find fauour.
32.15: He that seeketh the law, shall be filled therewith: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat.
32.16: They that feare the Lord shall find iudgement, and shall kindle iustice as a light.
32.17: A sinfull man will not be reproued, but findeth an excuse according to his will.
32.18: A man of counsell will be considerate, but a strange and proud man is not daunted with feare, euen when of himselfe he hath done without counsell.
32.19: Doe nothing without aduice, and when thou hast once done, repent not.
32.20: Goe not in a way wherein thou maiest fall, and stumble not among the stones.
32.21: Be not confident in a plaine way.
32.22: And beware of thine owne children.
32.23: In euery good worke trust thy owne soule: for this is the keeping of the commandements.
32.24: He that beleeueth in the Lord, taketh heed to the commandement, and he that trusted in him, shall fare neuer the worse.

33.1: There shall no euill happen vnto him that feareth the Lord, but in temptation euen againe he will deliuer him.
33.2: A wise man hateth not the Law, but he that is an hypocrite therein, is as a ship in a storme.
33.3: A man of vnderstanding trusteth in the Law, and the Law is faithfull vnto him, as an oracle.
33.4: Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard, and binde vp instruction, and then make answere.
33.5: The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheele: and his thoughts are like a rolling axeltree.
33.6: A stallion horse is as a mocking friend, hee neigheth vnder euery one that sitteth vpon him.
33.7: Why doth one day excell another? when as all the light of euery day in the yeere is of the Sunne.
33.8: By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
33.9: Some of them hath hee made high dayes, and hallowed them, and some of them hath hee made ordinary dayes.
33.10: And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.
33.11: In much knowledge the Lord hath diuided them, and made their wayes diuers.
33.12: Some of them hath hee blessed, and exalted, and some of them hath hee sanctified, and set neere himselfe: but some of them hath hee cursed, and brought low, and turned out of their places.
33.13: As the clay is in the potters hand to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
33.14: Good is set against euill, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
33.15: So looke vpon all the workes of the most High, and there are two and two, one against another.
33.16: I awaked vp last of all, as one that gathereth after the grape-gatherers: by the blessing of the Lord I profited, and filled my wine-presse, like a gatherer of grapes.
33.17: Consider that I laboured not for my selfe onely, but for all them that seeke learning;
33.18: Heare me, O ye great men of the people, and hearken with your eares ye rulers of the Congregation:
33.19: Giue not thy sonne, and wife, thy brother and friend power ouer thee while thou liuest, and giue not thy goods to another, lest it repent thee: and thou intreat for the same againe.
33.20: As long as thou liuest and hast breath in thee, giue not thy selfe ouer to any.
33.21: For better it is that thy children should seeke to thee, then that thou shouldst stand to their courtesie.
33.22: In all thy workes keepe to thy selfe the preheminence, leaue not a staine in thine honour.
33.23: At the time when thou shalt end thy dayes, and finish thy life, distribute thine inheritance.
33.24: Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the asse: and bread, correction, and worke for a seruant.
33.25: If thou set thy seruant to labour, thou shalt finde rest: but if thou let him goe idle, he shall seeke libertie.
33.26: A yoke and a collar doe bow the necke: so are tortures and torments for an euill seruant.
33.27: Sende him to labour that hee be not idle: for idlenesse teacheth much euill.
33.28: Set him to worke, as is fit for him; if he be not obedient, put on more heauy fetters.
33.29: But be not excessiue toward any, and without discretion doe nothing.
33.30: If thou haue a seruant, let him bee vnto thee as thy selfe, because thou hast bought him with a price.
33.31: If thou haue a seruant, intreate him as a brother: for thou hast neede of him, as of thine owne soule: if thou intreate him euill, and he runne from thee, which way wilt thou goe to seeke him?

34.1: The hopes of a man voyd of vnderstanding are vaine, and false: and dreames lift vp fooles.
34.2: Who so regardeth dreames, is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the winde.
34.3: The vision of dreames is the resemblance of one thing to another, euen as the likenesse of a face to a face.
34.4: Of an vncleane thing, what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false, what trueth can come?
34.5: Diuinations, and soothsayings, and dreames are vaine: and the heart fancieth as a womans heart in trauell.
34.6: If they be not sent from the most high in thy visitation, set not thy heart vpon them.
34.7: For dreames haue deceiued many, and they haue failed that put their trust in them.
34.8: The Law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisedome is perfection to a faithfull mouth.
34.9: A man that hath trauailed knoweth many things: and hee that hath much experience, wil declare wisedome.
34.10: He that hath no experience, knoweth little: but he that hath trauailed, is full of prudence.
34.11: When I trauailed, I saw many things: and I vnderstand more, then I can expresse.
34.12: I was oft times in danger of death, yet I was deliuered because of these things.
34.13: The spirit of those that feare the Lord shall liue, for their hope is in him that saueth them.
34.14: Who so feareth the Lord, shall not feare nor be afraid, for hee is his hope.
34.15: Blessed is the soule of him that feareth the Lord: to whom doeth hee looke? and who is his strength?
34.16: For the eyes of the Lord are vpon them that loue him, he is their mightie protection, and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a couer from the Sunne at noone, a preseruation from stumbling, and a helpe from falling.
34.17: He raiseth vp the soule, and lighteneth the eyes: hee giueth health, life, and blessing.
34.18: Hee that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous, and the giftes of vniust men are not accepted.
34.19: The most high is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked, neither is he pacified for sinne by the multitude of sacrifices.
34.20: Who so bringeth an offering of the goods of the poore, doeth as one that killeth the sonne before his fathers eyes.
34.21: The bread of the needie, is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof, is a man of blood.
34.22: Hee that taketh away his neighbours liuing, slayeth him: and hee that defraudeth the labourer of his hire, is a bloodshedder.
34.23: When one buildeth, and another pulleth downe, what profite haue they then but labour?
34.24: When one prayeth, and another curseth, whose voice will the Lorde heare?
34.25: He that washeth himselfe after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it againe, what auaileth his washing?
34.26: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sinnes, and goeth againe and doeth the same: who will heare his prayer, or what doeth his humbling profit him?

35.1: Hee that keepeth the law, bringeth offerings enow: he that taketh heed to the commandement, offereth a peace offering.
35.2: He that requiteth a good turne, offereth fine floure: and he that giueth almes, sacrificeth praise.
35.3: To depart from wickednesse is a thing pleasing to the Lord: and to forsake vnrighteousnesse, is a propitiation.
35.4: Thou shalt not appeare emptie before the Lord:
35.5: For all these things because of the commandement.
35.6: The offering of the righteous maketh the Altar fat, and the sweete sauour thereof is before the most high.
35.7: The sacrifice of a iust man is acceptable, and the memoriall thereof shall neuer be forgotten.
35.8: Giue the Lord his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the first fruits of thine hands.
35.9: In all thy gifts shew a cheerefull countenance, and dedicate thy tithes with gladnesse.
35.10: Giue vnto the most high, according as hee hath enriched thee, and as thou hast gotten, giue with a cheerefull eye.
35.11: For the Lord recompenseth, and will giue thee seuen times as much.
35.12: Doe not thinke to corrupt with gifts, for such he will not receiue: and trust not to vnrighteous sacrifices, for the Lord is iudge, and with him is no respect of persons.
35.13: Hee will not accept any person against a poore man: but will heare the prayer of the oppressed.
35.14: He will not despise the supplication of the fatherlesse: nor the widowe when she powreth out her complaint.
35.15: Doeth not the teares run downe the widowes cheeks? and is not her crie against him that causeth them to fall?
35.16: He that serueth the Lord, shall be accepted with fauour, and his prayer shall reach vnto the cloudes.
35.17: The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds: and till it come nigh he will not be comforted: and will not depart till the most High shall beholde to iudge righteously, and execute iudgement.
35.18: For the Lord wil not be slacke, neither will the mightie be patient towards them, till he hath smitten in sunder the loines of the vnmercifull, and repaid vengeance to the heathen: till he haue taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the scepter of the vnrighteous:
35.19: Till he haue rendred to euery man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their deuises, till he haue iudged the cause of his people: and made them to reioyce in his mercie,
35.20: Mercie is seasonable in the time of affliction, as cloudes of raine in the time of drought.

36.1: Haue mercie vpon vs, O Lord God of all, and behold vs:
36.2: And send thy feare vpon all the nations that seeke not after thee.
36.3: Lift vp thy hand against the strange nations, and let them see thy power.
36.4: As thou wast sanctified in vs before them: so be thou magnified among them before vs.
36.5: And let them know thee, as we haue knowen thee, that there is no God, but onely thou, O God.
36.6: Shew new signes, and make other strange wonders: glorifie thy hand and thy right arme, that they may set forth thy wonderous workes.
36.7: Raise vp indignation, and powre out wrath: take away the aduersarie and destroy the enemie.
36.8: Make the time short, remember the couenant, and let them declare thy wonderfull works.
36.9: Let him that escapeth, be consumed by the rage of the fire, and let them perish that oppresse the people.
36.10: Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.
36.11: Gather all the tribes of Iacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.
36.12: O Lord haue mercie vpon the people, that is called by thy name, and vpon Israel, whom thou hast named thy first borne.
36.13: O bee mercifull vnto Ierusalem thy holy citie, the place of thy rest.
36.14: Fill Sion with thine vnspeakable oracles, and thy people with thy glory.
36.15: Giue testimonie vnto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise vp prophets that haue bin in thy name.
36.16: Reward them that wait for thee, and let thy prophets be found faithfull.
36.17: O Lord heare the prayer of thy seruants, according to the blessing of Aaron ouer thy people, that all they which dwel vpon the earth, may know that thou art the Lord, the eternall God.
36.18: The belly deuoureth all meates, yet is one meat better then another.
36.19: As the palate tasteth diuers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of vnderstanding false speeches.
36.20: A froward heart causeth heauinesse: but a man of experience will recompense him.
36.21: A woman will receiue euery man, yet is one daughter better then another
36.22: The beautie of a woman cheareth the countenance, and a man loueth nothing better.
36.23: If there be kindnesse, meekenes, and comfort in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.
36.24: He that getteth a wife, beginneth a possession, a helpe like vnto himselfe, and a pillar of rest.
36.25: Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled: and he that hath no wife will wander vp and downe mourning.
36.26: Who will trust a thiefe well appointed, that skippeth from citie to citie? so a man that hath no house? and lodgeth wheresoeuer the night taketh him?

37.1: Euery friend saieth, I am his friend also: but there is a friend which is onely a friend in name.
37.2: Is it not a griefe vnto death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemie?
37.3: O wicked imagination, whence camest thou in to couer the earth with deceit?
37.4: There is a companion, which reioyceth in the prosperity of a friend: but in the time of trouble will be against him.
37.5: There is a companion which helpeth his friend for the belly, and taketh vp the buckler against the enemie.
37.6: Forget not thy friend in thy minde, and be not vnmindfull of him in thy riches.
37.7: Euery counseller extolleth counsell; but there is some that counselleth for himselfe.
37.8: Beware of a counseller, and know before what neede he hath (for he will counsell for himselfe) lest hee cast the lot vpon thee:
37.9: And say vnto thee, Thy way is good: and afterward he stand on the other side, to see what shall befall thee.
37.10: Consult not with one that suspecteth thee: and hide thy counsell from such as enuie thee.
37.11: Neither consult with a woman touching her of whom she is iealous; neither with a coward in matters of warre, nor with a merchant concerning exchange; nor with a buyer of selling; nor with an enuious man of thankfulnesse; nor with an vnmercifull man touching kindnesse; nor with the slouthfull for any worke; nor with an hireling for a yeere, of finishing worke; nor with an idle seruant of much businesse: Hearken not vnto these in any matter of counsell.
37.12: But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keepe the commandements of the Lord, whose minde is according to thy minde, and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry.
37.13: And let the counsell of thine owne heart stand: for there is no man more faithfull vnto thee then it.
37.14: For a mans minde is sometime wont to tell him more then seuen watchmen, that sit aboue in an high towre.
37.15: And aboue all this pray to the most high, that he will direct thy way in trueth.
37.16: Let reason goe before euery enterprise, & counsell before euery action.
37.17: The countenance is a signe of changing of the heart.
37.18: Foure maner of things appeare: good and euill, life and death: but the tongue ruleth ouer them continually.
37.19: There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is vnprofitable to himselfe.
37.20: There is one that sheweth wisedome in words, and is hated: he shall be destitute of all foode.
37.21: For grace is not giuen him from the Lord: because he is depriued of all wisedome.
37.22: Another is wise to himselfe: and the fruits of vnderstanding are commendable in his mouth.
37.23: A wise man instructeth his people, and the fruits of his vnderstanding faile not.
37.24: A wise man shall be filled with blessing, and all they that see him, shall count him happy.
37.25: The daies of the life of man may be numbred: but the daies of Israel are innumerable.
37.26: A wise man shall inherite glory among his people, and his name shalbe perpetuall.
37.27: My sonne prooue thy soule in thy life, and see what is euill for it, and giue not that vnto it.
37.28: For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath euery soule pleasure in euery thing.
37.29: Be not vnsatiable in any dainty thing: nor too greedy vpon meates.
37.30: For excesse of meates, bringeth sicknesse, and surfetting will turne into choler.
37.31: By surfetting haue many perished, but hee that taketh heed, prolongeth his life.

38.1: Honour a Phisitian with the honour due vnto him, for the vses which you may haue of him: for the Lord hath created him.
38.2: For of the most High commeth healing, and he shall receiue honour of the King.
38.3: The skill of the Phisitian shall lift vp his head: and in the sight of great men he shalbe in admiration.
38.4: The Lord hath created medicines out of the earth; and he that is wise will not abhorre them.
38.5: Was not the water made sweet with wood, that the vertue thereof might be knowen?
38.6: And he hath giuen men skill, that hee might be honoured in his marueilous workes.
38.7: With such doeth he heale and taketh away their paines.
38.8: Of such doeth the Apothecarie make a confection; and of his workes there is no end, and from him is peace ouer all the earth.
38.9: My sonne, in thy sickenesse be not negligent: but pray vnto the Lord, and he will make thee whole.
38.10: Leaue off from sinne, and order thy hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all wickednesse.
38.11: Giue a sweet sauour, and a memoriall of fine flowre: and make a fat offering, as not being.
38.12: Then giue place to the phisitian, for the Lord hath created him: let him not go from thee, for thou hast need of him.
38.13: There is a time when in their hands there is good successe.
38.14: For they shall also pray vnto the Lord, that hee would prosper that, which they giue, for ease and remedy to prolong life.
38.15: He that sinneth before his maker, let him fal into the hand of the Phisitian.
38.16: My sonne, let teares fall downe ouer the dead, and begin to lament, as if thou hadst suffered great harme thy selfe: and then couer his body according to the custome, & neglect not his buriall.
38.17: Weepe bitterly, and make great moane, and vse lamentation, as hee is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be euill spoken of: and then comfort thy selfe for thy heauinesse.
38.18: For of heauinesse commeth death, and the heauinesse of the heart, breaketh strength.
38.19: In affliction also sorrow remaineth: and the life of the poore, is the curse of the heart.
38.20: Take no heauines to heart: driue it away, and remember the last end.
38.21: Forget it not, for there is no turning againe: thou shalt not doe him good, but hurt thy selfe.
38.22: Remember my iudgement: for thine also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for thee.
38.23: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest, & be comforted for him, when his spirit is departed from him.
38.24: The wisedome of a learned man cōmeth by opportunitie of leasure: & he that hath litle busines shal become wise.
38.25: How can he get wisdome that holdeth the plough, and that glorieth in the goad; that driueth oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talke is of bullocks?
38.26: He giueth his minde to make furrowes: and is diligent to giue the kine fodder.
38.27: So euery carpenter, and workemaster, that laboureth night and day: and they that cut and graue seales, and are diligent to make great variety, and giue themselues to counterfait imagerie, and watch to finish a worke.
38.28: The smith also sitting by the anuill, & considering the iron worke; the vapour of the fire wasteth his flesh, and he fighteth with the heat of the furnace: the noise of the hammer & the anuill is euer in his eares, and his eies looke still vpon the patterne of the thing that he maketh, he setteth his mind to finish his worke, & watcheth to polish it perfitly.
38.29: So doeth the potter sitting at his worke, and turning the wheele about with his feet, who is alway carefully set at his worke: and maketh all his worke by number.
38.30: He fashioneth the clay with his arme, and boweth downe his strength before his feet: he applieth himselfe to lead it ouer; and he is diligent to make cleane the furnace.
38.31: All these trust to their hands: and euery one is wise in his worke.
38.32: Without these cannot a citie be inhabited: and they shall not dwell where they will, nor goe vp and downe.
38.33: They shall not be sought for in publike counsaile; nor sit high in the congregation: they shal not sit on the Iudges seate, nor vnderstand the sentence of iudgement: they cannot declare iustice, and iudgement, and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.
38.34: But they will maintaine the state of the world, and their desire is in the worke of their craft.

39.1: But hee that giueth his minde to the Law of the most high, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, wil seeke out the wisdome of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.
39.2: Hee will keepe the sayings of the renowmed men: and where subtile parables are, he will be there also.
39.3: Hee will seeke out the secrets of graue sentences, and be conuersant in darke parables.
39.4: He shall serue among great men, and appeare before princes: he will trauaile through strange countreys, for hee hath tried the good, and the euill among men.
39.5: Hee will giue his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and will pray before the most high, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sinnes.
39.6: When the great Lord will, he shall bee filled with the spirit of vnderstanding: he shal powre out wise sentences, and giue thankes vnto the Lord in his prayer.
39.7: Hee shall direct his counsell and knowledge, and in his secrets shall hee meditate.
39.8: Hee shall shew foorth that which he hath learned, and shall glory in the Law of the couenant of the Lord.
39.9: Many shall commend his vnderstanding, and so long as the world endureth, it shall not be blotted out, his memoriall shall not depart away, and his name shall liue from generation to generation.
39.10: Nations shall shewe foorth his wisedome, and the congregation shall declare his praise.
39.11: If hee die, he shall leaue a greater name then a thousand: and if he liue, he shall increase it.
39.12: Yet I haue more to say which I haue thought vpon, for I am filled as the Moone at the full.
39.13: Hearken vnto me, ye holy children, and budde foorth as a rose growing by the brooke of the field:
39.14: And giue yee a sweete sauour as frankincense, and flourish as a lilly, send foorth a smell, and sing a song of praise, blesse the Lord in all his workes.
39.15: Magnifie his Name, and shewe foorth his praise with the songs of your lips, and with harpes, and in praising him you shall say after this maner:
39.16: Al the works of the Lord are exceeding good, & whatsoeuer hee commandeth, shalbe accomplished in due season.
39.17: And none may say, What is this? wherefore is that? for at time conuenient they shall all be sought out: at his commaundement the waters stood as an heape, & at the wordes of his mouth the receptacles of waters.
39.18: At his commandement is done whatsoeuer pleaseth him, and none can hinder when he will saue.
39.19: The workes of all flesh are before him, & nothing can be hid from his eyes.
39.20: He seeth from euerlasting to euerlasting, and there is nothing wonderfull before him.
39.21: A man neede not to say, What is this? wherefore is that? for hee hath made all things for their vses.
39.22: His blessing couered the dry land as a riuer, and watered it as a flood.
39.23: As hee hath turned the waters into saltnesse: so shall the heathen inherite his wrath.
39.24: As his wayes are plaine vnto the holy, so are they stumbling blockes vnto the wicked.
39.25: For the good, are good things created from the beginning: so euill things for sinners.
39.26: The principall things for the whole vse of mans life, are water, fire, yron, and salt, floure of wheate, honie, milke, and the blood of the grape, and oyle, and clothing.
39.27: All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into euill.
39.28: There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their furie lay on sore strokes, in the time of destruction they powre out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.
39.29: Fire, and haile, and famine, and death: all these were created for vengeance:
39.30: Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, & the sword, punishing the wicked to destruction.
39.31: They shall reioice in his commandement, and they shall bee ready vpon earth when neede is, and when their time is come, they shall not transgresse his word.
39.32: Therefore from the beginning I was resolued, and thought vpon these things, and haue left them in writing.
39.33: All the workes of the Lord are good: and he will giue euery needefull thing in due season.
39.34: So that a man cannot say, This is worse then that: for in time they shall all be well approued.
39.35: And therefore praise ye the Lord with the whole heart and mouth, and blesse the Name of the Lord.

40.1: Great trauaile is created for euery man, and an heauy yoke is vpon the sons of Adam, from the day that they goe out of their mothers wombe, till the day that they returne to the mother of all things.
40.2: Their imagination of things to come, & the day of death their thoughts, and feare of heart:
40.3: From him that sitteth on a throne of glory, vnto him that is humbled in earth and ashes.
40.4: From him that weareth purple, and a crown, vnto him that is clothed with a linnen frocke.
40.5: Wrath, and enuie, trouble and vnquietnesse, feare of death, and anger, and strife, and in the time of rest vpon his bed, his night sleepe doe change his knowledge.
40.6: A litle or nothing is his rest, and afterward he is in his sleepe, as in a day of keeping watch, troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he were escaped out of a battell:
40.7: When all is safe, he awaketh, and marueileth that the feare was nothing.
40.8: vnto all flesh, both man and beast, and that is seuen fold more vpon sinners.
40.9: Death and bloodshed, strife and sword, calamities, famine, tribulation, and the scourge:
40.10: These things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.
40.11: All things that are of the earth shal turne to the earth againe: and that which is of the waters doeth returne into the Sea.
40.12: All briberie and iniustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for euer.
40.13: The goods of the vniust shall bee dried vp like a riuer, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in raine.
40.14: While he openeth his hand he shal reioyce: so shall transgressours come to nought.
40.15: The children of the vngodly shall not bring forth many branches: but are as vncleane roots vpon a hard rocke.
40.16: The weed growing vpon euery water, and banke of a riuer, shall bee pulled vp before all grasse.
40.17: Bountifulnes is as a most fruitfull garden, and mercifulnesse endureth for euer.
40.18: To labour & to be content with that a man hath, is a sweet life: but hee that findeth a treasure, is aboue them both.
40.19: Children and the building of a citie continue a mans name: but a blamelesse wife is counted aboue them both.
40.20: Wine & musicke reioyce the heart: but the loue of wisedome is aboue them both.
40.21: The pipe and the psalterie make sweet melodie: but a pleasant tongue is aboue them both.
40.22: Thine eye desireth fauour and beautie: but more then both, corne while it is greene.
40.23: A friend and companion neuer meet amisse: but aboue both is a wife with her husband.
40.24: Brethren and helpe are against time of trouble: but almes shall deliuer more then them both.
40.25: Golde and siluer make the foote stand sure: but counsell is esteemed aboue them both.
40.26: Riches and strength lift vp the heart: but the feare of the Lord is aboue them both: there is no want in the feare of the Lord, and it needeth not to seeke helpe.
40.27: The feare of the Lord is a fruitfull garden, and couereth him aboue all glory.
40.28: My sonne, lead not a beggers life: for better it is to die then to beg.
40.29: The life of him that dependeth on another mans table, is not to be counted for a life: for he polluteth himselfe with other mens meate, but a wise man well nurtured will beware thereof.
40.30: Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shamelesse: but in his belly there shall burne a fire.

41.1: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liueth at rest in his possessions, vnto the man that hath nothing to vexe him, and that hath prosperity in all things: yea vnto him that is yet able to receiue meate?
41.2: O death, acceptable is thy sentence vnto the needy, and vnto him whose strength faileth, that is now in the last age, and is vexed with all things, and to him that despaireth and hath lost patience.
41.3: Feare not the sentence of death, remember them that haue beene before thee, and that come after, for this is the sentence of the Lord ouer all flesh.
41.4: And why art thou against the pleasure of the most High? there is no inquisition in the graue, whether thou haue liued ten, or a hundred, or a thousand yeeres.
41.5: The children of sinners, are abhominable children: and they that are conuersant in the dwelling of the vngodly.
41.6: The inheritance of sinners children shal perish, and their posterity shal haue a perpetuall reproch.
41.7: The children will complaine of an vngodly father, because they shall be reproched for his sake.
41.8: Woe be vnto you vngodly men which haue forsaken the law of the most high God: for if you encrease, it shall be to your destruction.
41.9: And if you be borne, you shall be borne to a curse: and if you die, a curse shall be your portion.
41.10: All that are of the earth shall turne to earth againe: so the vngodly shall goe from a curse to destruction.
41.11: The mourning of men is about their bodies: but an ill name of sinners shall be blotted out.
41.12: Haue regard to thy name: for that shall continue with thee aboue a thousand great treasures of gold.
41.13: A good life hath but few daies: but a good name endureth for euer.
41.14: My children, keepe discipline in peace: for wisedome that is hid, and a treasure that is not seene, what profit is in them both?
41.15: A man that hideth his foolishnesse is better then a man that hideth his wisedome.
41.16: Therefore be shamefast according to my word: for it is not good to retaine all shamefastnesse, neither is it altogether approoued in euery thing.
41.17: Be ashamed of whoredome before father and mother, and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man:
41.18: Of an offence before a iudge and ruler, of iniquitie before a congregation and people, of vniust dealing before thy partner and friend:
41.19: And of theft in regard of the place where thou soiournest, and in regard of the trueth of God and his couenant, and to leane with thine elbow vpon the meate, and of scorning to giue and take:
41.20: And of silence before them that salute thee, and to look vpon an harlot:
41.21: And to turne away thy face from thy kinsman, or to take away a portion or a gift, or to gaze vpon another mans wife,
41.22: Or to bee ouerbusie with his maide, and come not neere her bed, or of vpbraiding speaches before friends; and after thou hast giuen, vpbraide not:
41.23: Or of iterating and speaking againe that which thou hast heard, and of reuealing of secrets.
41.24: So shalt thou be truely shamefast, and finde fauour before all men.

42.1: Of these things be not thou ashamed, and accept no person to sinne thereby.
42.2: Of the Law of the most High, and his Couenant, and of iudgement to iustifie the vngodly:
42.3: Of reckoning with thy partners, and traueilers: or of the gift of the heritage of friends:
42.4: Of exactnesse of ballance, and waights: or of getting much or little:
42.5: And of merchants indifferent selling, of much correction of children, and to make the side of an euill seruant to bleed.
42.6: Sure keeping is good where an euill wife is, and shut vp where many hands are.
42.7: Deliuer all things in number and waight, and put al in writing that thou giuest out, or receiuest in.
42.8: Be not ashamed to informe the vnwise and foolish, and the extreeme aged that contendeth with those that are yong, thus shalt thou bee truely learned and approued of all men liuing.
42.9: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth, and the care for her taketh away sleepe; when shee is yong lest shee passe away the flowre of her age, and being married, lest she should be hated:
42.10: In her virginitie lest she should be defiled, and gotten with childe in her fathers house; and hauing an husband, lest she should misbehaue herselfe: and when shee is married, lest shee should be barren.
42.11: Keepe a sure watch ouer a shamelesse daughter, lest shee make thee a laughing stocke to thine enemies, and a by-word in the citie, and a reproch among the people, and make thee ashamed before the multitude.
42.12: Behold not euery bodies beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.
42.13: For from garments commeth a moth, and from women wickednesse.
42.14: Better is the churlishnesse of a man, then a courteous woman, a woman I say, which bringeth shame and reproch.
42.15: I will now remember the works of the Lord, and declare the things that I haue seene: in the words of the Lord are his workes.
42.16: The Sunne that giueth light, looketh vpon all things: and the worke thereof is full of the glory of the Lord.
42.17: The Lord hath not giuen power to the Saints to declare all his marueilous workes, which the Almightie Lord firmely setled, that whatsoeuer is, might be established for his glory.
42.18: He seeketh out the deepe and the heart, and considereth their crafty deuices: for the Lord knoweth all that may be knowen, and he beholdeth the signes of the world.
42.19: Hee declareth the things that are past, and for to come, and reueileth the steps of hidden things.
42.20: No thought escapeth him, neither any word is hidden from him.
42.21: Hee hath garnished the excellent workes of his wisedome, and hee is from euerlasting to euerlasting, vnto him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he hath no need of any counseller.
42.22: O how desireable are all his workes: and that a man may see euen to a sparke.
42.23: All these things liue and remaine for euer, for all vses, and they are all obedient.
42.24: All things are double one against another: and hee hath made nothing vnperfit.
42.25: One thing establisheth the good of another: and who shalbe filled with beholding his glory?

43.1: The pride of the height, the cleare firmament, the beautie of heauen, with his glorious shew;
43.2: The Sunne when it appeareth, declaring at his rising, a marueilous instrument, the worke of the most High.
43.3: At noone it parcheth the country, and who can abide the burning heate thereof?
43.4: A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the Sunne burneth the mountaines three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending foorth bright beames, it dimmeth the eyes.
43.5: Great is the Lord that made it, and at his commandement it runneth hastily.
43.6: He made the Moone also to serue in her season, for a declaration of times, and a signe of the world.
43.7: From the Moone is the signe of Feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.
43.8: The moneth is called after her name, encreasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies aboue, shining in the firmament of heauen,
43.9: The beautie of heauen, the glory of the starres, an ornament giuing light in the highest places of the Lord.
43.10: At the commandement of the holy One, they will stand in their order, and neuer faint in their watches.
43.11: Looke vpon the rainebow, and praise him that made it, very beautifull it is in the brightnesse thereof.
43.12: It compasseth the heauen about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most high haue bended it.
43.13: By his commandement hee maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth swiftly the lightnings of his iudgment.
43.14: Through this the treasures are opened, and clouds flie forth as foules.
43.15: By his great power hee maketh the cloudes firme, and the hailestones are broken small.
43.16: At his sight the mountaines are shaken, and at his will the South wind bloweth.
43.17: The noise of the thunder maketh the earth to tremble: so doth the Northren storme, and the whirlewinde: as birds flying he scattereth the snow, and the falling downe thereof, is as the lighting of grashoppers.
43.18: The eye marueileth at the beauty of the whitenesse thereof, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it.
43.19: The hoare frost also as salt hee powreth on the earth, and being congealed, it lieth on the toppe of sharpe stakes.
43.20: Wheu the colde North-winde bloweth, and the water is congealed into yce, it abideth vpon euery gathering together of water, and clotheth the water as with a brestplate.
43.21: It deuoureth the mountaines, and burneth the wildernesse, and consumeth the grasse as fire.
43.22: A present remedy of all is a miste comming speedily: a dew comming after heate, refresheth.
43.23: By his counsell he appeaseth the deepe, and planteth Ilands therein.
43.24: They that saile on the Sea, tell of the danger thereof, and when wee heare it with our eares, wee marueile thereat.
43.25: For therein be strange and wonderous workes, varietie of all kindes of beasts, and whales created.
43.26: By him the ende of them hath prosperous successe, and by his word all things consist.
43.27: We may speake much, & yet come short: wherefore in summe, he is all.
43.28: How shall wee be able to magnifie him? for hee is great aboue all his workes.
43.29: The Lord is terrible and very great, and marueilous is his power.
43.30: When you glorifie the Lord exalt him as much as you can: for euen yet wil he farre exceed, and when you exalt him, put foorth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can neuer goe farre enough.
43.31: Who hath seene him, that hee might tell vs? and who can magnifie him as he is?
43.32: There are yet hid greater things then these be, for wee haue seene but a few of his workes:
43.33: For the Lord hath made all things, and to the godly hath hee giuen wisedome.

44.1: Let vs now praise famous men, and our Fathers that begat vs.
44.2: The Lorde hath wrought great glory by them, through his great power from the beginning.
44.3: Such as did beare rule in their kingdomes, men renowmed for their power, giuing counsell by their vnderstanding, and declaring prophecies:
44.4: Leaders of the people by their counsels, and learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instructions.
44.5: Such as found out musical tunes, and reiected verses in writing.
44.6: Rich men furnished with abilitie, liuing peaceably in their habitations.
44.7: All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.
44.8: There be of them, that haue left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported.
44.9: And some there be, which haue no memorial, who are perished as though they had neuer bene, and are become as though they had neuer bene borne, and their children after them.
44.10: But these were mercifull men, whose righteousnesse hath not beene forgotten.
44.11: With their seed shall continually remaine a good inheritance, and their children are within the couenant.
44.12: Their seed stands fast, and their children for their sakes.
44.13: Their seed shall remaine for euer, and their glory shall not be blotted out.
44.14: Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name liueth for euermore.
44.15: The people will tell of their wisdome, and the congregation will shew forth their praise.
44.16: Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance, to all generations.
44.17: Noah was found perfect and righteous, in the time of wrath, he was taken in exchange (for the world) therefore was he left as a remnant vnto the earth, when the flood came.
44.18: An euerlasting Couenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.
44.19: Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like vnto him:
44.20: Who kept the Law of the most High, and was in couenant with him, hee established the Couenant in his flesh, and when he was proued, he was found faithfull.
44.21: Therefore he assured him by an othe, that he would blesse the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him, as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the starres, and cause them to inherit from Sea to Sea, & from the riuer vnto the vtmost part of the land.
44.22: With Isaac did he establish likewise the blessing of all men and the couenant,
44.23: And made it rest vpon the head of Iacob. Hee acknowledged him in his blessing, and gaue him an heritage, and diuided his portions, among the twelue tribes did he part them.

45.1: And he brought out of him a mercifull man, which found fauour in the sight of all flesh, euen Moses beloued of God and men, whose memoriall is blessed:
45.2: He made him like to the glorious Saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in feare of him.
45.3: By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gaue him a commaundement for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.
45.4: He sanctified him in his faithfulnesse, and meekenesse, and chose him out of all men.
45.5: He made him to heare his voyce, and brought him into the darke cloud, and gaue him commandements before his face, euen the law of life and knowledge, that hee might teach Iacob his Couenants, and Israel his iudgments.
45.6: He exalted Aaron an holy man like vnto him, euen his brother, of the tribe of Leui.
45.7: An euerlasting couenant he made with him, and gaue him the priesthood among the people, he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.
45.8: Hee put vpon him perfect glory: and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the Ephod:
45.9: And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bels round about, that as he went, there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the Temple, for a memoriall to the children of his people.
45.10: With an holy garment, with gold and blew silke, and purple the worke of the embroiderer; with a brestplate of iudgement, and with Urim & Thummim.
45.11: With twisted scarlet, the worke of the cunning workeman, with precious stones grauen like seales, and set in gold, the worke of the Ieweller, with a writing engraued for a memoriall, after the number of the tribes of Israel.
45.12: He set a crowne of gold vpon the miter, wherein was engraued holinesse an ornament of honour, a costly worke, the desires of the eies goodly & beautiful.
45.13: Before him there were none such, neither did euer any stranger put them on, but onely his children, and his childrens children perpetually.
45.14: Their sacrifices shall be wholy consumed euery day twise continually.
45.15: Moises consecrated him, and annointed him with holy oile, this was appointed vnto him by an euerlasting couenant, and to his seed so long as the heauens should remaine, that they should minister vnto him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and blesse the people in his name.
45.16: He chose him out of all men liuing to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense and a sweet sauour, for a memoriall, to make reconciliation for his people.
45.17: He gaue vnto him his commandements, and authority in the statutes of iudgements, that he should teach Iacob the testimonies, and informe Israel in his lawes.
45.18: Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wildernesse, euen the men that were of Dathans, and Abirons side, and the congregation of Core with fury and wrath.
45.19: This the Lord saw and it displeased him, and in his wrathfull indignation, were they consumed: he did wonders vpon them, to consume them with the fiery flame.
45.20: But he made Aaron more honourable, and gaue him an heritage, and diuided vnto him the first fruits of the encrease, especially he prepared bread in abundance:
45.21: For they eate of the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gaue vnto him and his seed:
45.22: Howbeit in the land of the people he had no inheritance, neither had he any portion among the people, for the Lord himselfe is his portion and inheritance.
45.23: The third in glory is Phinees the sonne of Eleazar, because he had zeale in the feare of the Lord, and stood vp with good courage of heart, when the people were turned backe, and made reconciliation for Israel.
45.24: Therfore was there a couenant of peace made with him, that he should be the cheefe of the sanctuary, and of his people, and that he, and his posteritie should haue the dignitie of the Priesthood for euer.
45.25: According to the couenant made with Dauid sonne of Iesse, of the tribe of Iuda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be vnto his seed.
45.26: God giue you wisedome in your heart to iudge his people in righteousnesse, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for euer.

46.1: Iesus the sonne of Naue was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophesies, who according to his name was made great for the sauing of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose vp against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance.
46.2: How great glory gat he when he did lift vp his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities?
46.3: Who before him so stood to it? for the Lord himselfe brought his enemies vnto him.
46.4: Did not the Sunne goe backe by his meanes? and was not one day as long as two?
46.5: He called vpon the most high Lord, when the enemies pressed vpon him on euery side, & the great Lord heard him.
46.6: And with hailestones of mighty power he made the battell to fall violently vpon the nations, and in the descent (of Bethoron) hee destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength, because hee fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the mightie one.
46.7: In the time of Moses also, he did a worke of mercie, hee and Caleb the sonne of Iephunne, in that they withstood the Congregation, and withheld the people from sinne, and appeased the wicked murmuring.
46.8: And of sixe hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserued to bring them into the heritage, euen vnto the land that floweth with milk & hony.
46.9: The Lord gaue strength also vnto Caleb, which remained with him vnto his old age, so that he entred vpon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage.
46.10: That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
46.11: And concerning the Iudges, euery one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed.
46.12: Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honoured, be continued vpon their children.
46.13: Samuel the Prophet of the Lord, beloued of his Lord, established a kingdom, & anointed princes ouer his people.
46.14: By the Law of the Lord hee iudged the Congregation, and the Lord had respect vnto Iacob.
46.15: By his faithfulnes he was found a true Prophet, and by his word he was knowen to be faithfull in vision.
46.16: He called vpon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed vpon him on euery side, when he offered the sucking lambe.
46.17: And the Lord thundered from heauen, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.
46.18: And he destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, and all the princes of the Philistines.
46.19: And before his long sleepe hee made protestations in the sight of the Lord, and his anoynted, I haue not taken any mans goods, so much as a shoe, and no man did accuse him.
46.20: And after his death he prophesied, and shewed the King his end, and lift vp his voyce from the earth in prophesie, to blot out the wickednesse of the people.

47.1: And after him rose vp Nathan to prophesie in the time of Dauid.
47.2: As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was Dauid chosen out of the children of Israel.
47.3: Hee played with Lions as with kids, and with beares as with lambs.
47.4: Slew he not a gyant when hee was yet but yong? and did he not take away reproch from the people, when he lifted vp his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat downe the boasting of Goliah?
47.5: For he called vpon the most high Lord, and he gaue him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warriour, and set vp the horne of his people:
47.6: So the people honoured him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in that hee gaue him a crowne of glory.
47.7: For hee destroyed the enemies on euery side, and brought to nought the Philistines his aduersaries, and brake their horne in sunder vnto this day.
47.8: In all his workes hee praised the holy one most High, with words of glory, with his whole heart he sung songs, and loued him that made him.
47.9: He set singers also before the Altar, that by their voyces they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs.
47.10: He beautified their feasts, and set in order the solemne times, vntill the ende, that they might praise his holy Name, and that the Temple might sound from morning.
47.11: The Lord tooke away his sinnes, and exalted his horne for euer: he gaue him a couenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.
47.12: After him rose vp a wise sonne, and for his sake he dwelt at large.
47.13: Salomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that hee might build an house in his Name, and prepare his Sanctuary for euer.
47.14: How wise wast thou in thy youth, & as a flood filled with vnderstanding.
47.15: Thy soule couered the whole earth, and thou filledst it with dark parables.
47.16: Thy name went farre vnto the Ilands, and for thy peace thou wast beloued.
47.17: The countreys marueiled at thee for thy Songs, and Prouerbs, and Parables, and interpretations.
47.18: By the Name of the Lord God, which is called the Lord God of Israel, thou didst gather gold as tinne, and didst multiply siluer as lead.
47.19: Thou didst bow thy loines vnto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subiection.
47.20: Thou dist staine thy honour, and pollute thy seed, so that thou broughtest wrath vpon thy children, and wast grieued for thy folly.
47.21: So the kingdome was diuided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdome.
47.22: But the Lord will neuer leaue off his mercy, neither shall any of his workes perish, neither will hee abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loueth him he will not take away: wherefore he gaue a remnant vnto Iacob, and out of him a roote vnto Dauid.
47.23: Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seede he left behinde him Roboam, euen the foolishnesse of the people, and one that had no vnderstanding; who turned away the people through his counsell: there was also Ieroboam the sonne of Nabat, who caused Israel to sinne, and shewed Ephraim the way of sinne:
47.24: And their sinnes were multiplied exceedingly, that they were driuen out of the land.
47.25: For they sought out all wickednes, till the vengeance came vpon them.

48.1: Then stood vp Elias the Prophet as fire, and his word burnt like a lampe.
48.2: He brought a sore famine vpon them, and by his zeale he diminished their number.
48.3: By the word of the Lord he shut vp the heauen, and also three times brought downe fire.
48.4: O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deedes! and who may glory like vnto thee!
48.5: Who didst raise vp a dead man from death, & his soule from the place of the dead by the word of the most Hie.
48.6: Who broughtest kings to destruction, and honourable men from their bedde.
48.7: Who heardest the rebuke of the Lord in Sinai, and in Horeb the iudgment of vengeance.
48.8: Who anointed kings to take reuenge, & Prophets to succeed after him:
48.9: Who wast taken vp in a whirlewinde of fire, and in a charet of fierie horses:
48.10: Who wast ordained for reproofes in their times, to pacifie the wrath of the Lordes iudgement before it brake foorth into fury, and to turne the heart of the father vnto the sonne, and to restore the tribes of Iacob.
48.11: Blessed are they that saw thee, and slept in loue, for we shal surely liue.
48.12: Elias it was, who was couered with a whirlewinde: and Elizeus was filled with his spirit: whilest he liued he was not mooued of any prince, neither could any bring him into subiection.
48.13: No word could ouercome him, & after his death his body prophecied.
48.14: He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marueilous.
48.15: For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sinnes, till they were spoiled and caried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of Dauid:
48.16: Of whom, some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sinnes.
48.17: Ezekias fortified his citie, and brought in water into the midst thereof: he digged the hard rocke with yron, and made welles for waters.
48.18: In his time Sennacherib came vp, and sent Rabsaces, and lift vp his hand against Sion, & boasted proudly.
48.19: Then trembled their hearts and handes, and they were in paine as women in trauell.
48.20: But they called vpon the Lord which is mercifull, and stretched out their hands towards him, and immediatly the holy One heard them out of heauen, and deliuered them by the ministery of Esay.
48.21: He smote the hoste of the Assyrians, and his Angel destroyed them.
48.22: For Ezekias had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the wayes of Dauid his father, as Esay the Prophet, who was great and faithfull in his vision, had commaunded him.
48.23: In his time the Sunne went backeward, and hee lengthened the kings life.
48.24: Hee sawe by an excellent spirit what should come to passe at the last, and hee comforted them that mourned in Sion.
48.25: He shewed what should come to passe for euer, and secret things or euer they came.

49.1: The remembrance of Iosias is like the composition of the perfume þt is made by the arte of the Apothecarie: it is sweete as hony in all mouthes, and as musicke at a banquet of wine.
49.2: He behaued himselfe vprightly in the conuersion of the people, and tooke away the abominations of iniquitie.
49.3: He directed his heart vnto the Lord, and in the time of the vngodly he established the worship of God.
49.4: All, except Dauid and Ezechias, and Iosias, were defectiue: for they forsooke the Law of the most High, (euen) the kings of Iudah failed:
49.5: Therefore he gaue their power vnto others, & their glory to a strange nation.
49.6: They burnt the chosen citie of the Sanctuarie, and made the streets desolate according to the prophecie of Ieremias:
49.7: For they entreated him euil, who neuerthelesse was a prophet sanctified in his mothers wombe, that he might root out and afflict & destroy, and that he might build vp also and plant.
49.8: It was Ezechiel who sawe the glorious vision, which was shewed him vpon the chariot of the Cherubims
49.9: For he made mention of the enemies vnder the raine, and directed them that went right.
49.10: And of the twelue prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish againe out of their place: for they comforted Iacob, and deliuered them by assured hope.
49.11: How shall we magnifie Zorobabel? euen he was as a signet on the right hand.
49.12: So was Iesus the sonne of Iosedec: who in their time builded the house, and set vp an holy Temple to the Lord, which was prepared for euerlasting glory.
49.13: And among the elect was Neemias whose renowme is great, who raised vp for vs, the walles that were fallen, and set vp the gates & the barres, and raised vp our ruines againe.
49.14: But vpon the earth was no man created like Enoch, for he was taken from the earth.
49.15: Neither was there a man borne like vnto Ioseph, a gouernour of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.
49.16: Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam aboue euery liuing thing in the creation.

50.1: Simon the high priest the sonne of Onias, who in his life repaired the house againe, and in his dayes fortified the Temple:
50.2: And by him was built from the foundation the double height, the high fortresse of the wall about the Temple.
50.3: In his dayes the cisterne to receiue water being in compasse as the sea, was couered with plates of brasse.
50.4: He tooke care of the Temple that it should not fall, and fortified the citie against besieging.
50.5: How was he honoured in the midst of the people, in his comming out of the Sanctuarie?
50.6: He was as the morning starre in the midst of a cloud: and as the moone at the full.
50.7: As the Sunne shining vpon the Temple of the most High, and as the rainebow giuing light in the bright cloudes.
50.8: And as the flowre of roses in the spring of the yeere, as lillies by the riuers of waters, and as the branches of the frankincense tree in the time of summer.
50.9: As fire and incense in the censer, and as a vessell of beaten gold set with all maner of precious stones,
50.10: And as a faire oliue tree budding forth fruit, and as a Cypresse tree which groweth vp to the cloudes.
50.11: When he put on the robe of honour, and was clothed with the perfection of glory, when he went vp to the holy altar, he made the garment of holinesse honourable.
50.12: When he tooke the portions out of the priests hands, hee himselfe stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed with his brethren round about, as a yong cedar in Libanus, and as palme trees compassed they him round about.
50.13: So were all the sonnes of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of the Lord in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel.
50.14: And finishing the seruice at the altar, that he might adorne the offring of the most high Almighty,
50.15: He stretched out his hand to the cup, and powred of the blood of the grape, he powred out at the foote of the altar, a sweet smelling sauour vnto the most high King of all.
50.16: Then shouted the sonnes of Aaron, and sounded the siluer trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the most High.
50.17: Then all the people together hasted, and fell downe to the earth vpon their faces to worship their Lord God almighty the most High.
50.18: The singers also sang praises with their voices, with great variety of sounds was there made sweete melodie.
50.19: And the people besought the Lord the most High by prayer before him that is mercifull, till the solemnity of the Lord was ended, and they had finished his seruice.
50.20: Then he went downe, and lifted vp his hands ouer the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to giue the blessing of the Lord with his lips, and to reioyce in his name.
50.21: And they bowed themselues downe to worship the second time, that they might receiue a blessing from the most High.
50.22: Now therefore blesse yee the God of all, which onely doth wonderous things euery where, which exalteth our daies from the wombe, and dealeth with vs according to his mercy.
50.23: He grant vs ioyfulnesse of heart, and that peace may be in our daies in Israel for euer.
50.24: That hee would confirme his mercy with vs, and deliuer vs at his time.
50.25: There be two maner of nations which my heart abhorreth, and the third is no nation.
50.26: They that sit vpon the mountaine of Samaria, and they that dwell amongst the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.
50.27: Iesus the sonne of Sirach of Hierusalem hath written in this booke, the instruction of vnderstanding and knowledge, who out of his heart powred forth wisedome.
50.28: Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things, and hee that layeth them vp in his heart, shall become wise.
50.29: For if he doe them, hee shall be strong to all things, for the light of the Lord leadeth him, who giueth wisedome to the godly: blessed be the Lord for euer. Amen. Amen.

51.1: I will thanke thee, O Lord and king, and praise thee O God my Sauiour, I doe giue praise vnto thy name:
51.2: For thou art my defeuder, and helper, and hast preserued my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lippes that forge lies, and hast beene my helper against mine aduersaries.
51.3: And hast deliuered me according to the multitude of thy mercies, and greatnesse of thy name, from the teeth of them that were ready to deuoure me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had:
51.4: From the choking of fire on euery side, and from the mids of the fire, which I kindled not:
51.5: From the depth of the belly of hel, from an vncleane tongue, and from lying words.
51.6: By an accusation to the king from an vnrighteous tongue, my soule drew neere euen vnto death, my life was neere to the hell beneath:
51.7: They compassed me on euery side, and there was no man to helpe me: I looked for the succour of men, but there was none:
51.8: Then thought I vpon thy mercy, O Lord, and vpon thy acts of old, how thou deliuerest such as waite for thee, and sauest them out of the hands of the enemies:
51.9: Then lifted I vp my supplication from the earth, and prayed for deliuerance from death.
51.10: I called vpon the Lord the father of my Lord, that he would not leaue me in the dayes of my trouble, & in the time of the proud when there was no helpe.
51.11: I will praise thy Name continually, and will sing praise with thankesgiuing, and so my prayer was heard:
51.12: For thou sauedst me from destruction, and deliuerest mee from the euill time: therefore will I giue thankes and praise thee, and blesse thy Name, O Lord.
51.13: When I was yet yong, or euer I went abroad, I desired wisedome openly in my prayer.
51.14: I prayed for her before the Temple, & will seeke her out euen to the end:
51.15: Euen from the flowre till the grape was ripe, hath my heart delighted in her, my foot went the right way, from my youth vp sought I after her.
51.16: I bowed downe mine eare a litle and receiued her, & gate much learning.
51.17: I profited therein, will I ascribe the glory vnto him that giueth me wisedome:
51.18: For I purposed to doe after her, and earnestly I followed that which is good, so shall I not be confounded:
51.19: My soule hath wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact, I stretched foorth my hands to the heauen aboue, & bewailed my ignorances of her.
51.20: I directed my soule vnto her, and I found her in purenesse, I haue had my heart ioyned with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not bee forsaken.
51.21: My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore haue I gotten a good possession.
51.22: The Lord hath giuen mee a tongue for my reward, and I wil praise him therewith.
51.23: Draw neere vnto me you vnlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.
51.24: Wherefore are you slow, and what say you of these things, seeing your soules are very thirstie?
51.25: I opened my mouth, and said, buy her for your selues without money.
51.26: Put your necke vnder the yoke, and let your soule receiue instruction, she is hard at hand to finde.
51.27: Behold with your eies, how that I haue had but little labour, and haue gotten vnto me much rest.
51.28: Get learning with a great summe of money, and get much gold by her.
51.29: Let your soule reioyce in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise.
51.30: Worke your worke betimes, & in his time he will giue you your reward.

0.0: προλοΓοϲ ΠΟΛΛΩΝ καὶ μεγάλων ἡμῖν διὰ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων τῶν κατʼ αὐτούς ἠκολουθηκότων δεδομένων, ὑπὲρ ὧν δέον ἐστὶν ἐπαινεῖν τὸν Ἰσραὴλ παιδείας καὶ σοφίας· καὶ ὡς οὐ μόνον αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἀναγινώσκοντας δέον ἐστὶν ἐπιστήμονας γίνεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς ἐκτὸς δύνασθαι τοὺς φιλομαθοῦντας χρησίμους εἴψαι καὶ λέγοντας καὶ γράφοντας· ὁ πάππος μου Ἰησοῦς ἐπὶ πλεῖὸν ἑαυτὸν δοὺς εἴς τε τὴν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων πατρίων βιβλίων ἀνάγνωσιν, καὶ ἐν τούτοις ἱκανὴν ἔξιν περιποιησάμενος, προήχθη καὶ αὐτὸς συγγράψαι τι τῶν εἰς παιδείαν καὶ σοφίαν ἀνηκόντων, ὅπως οἱ φιλομαθεῖς καὶ τούτων ἔνοχοι γενόμενοι πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐπιπροσθῶσιν διὰ τῆς ἐννόμου βιώσεως. παρακέκλησθε οὖν μετʼ εὐνοίας καΣ προσοχῆς τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν ποιεῖσθαι, καὶ συγγνώμην ἔχειν ἐφʼ οἰς ἂν δοκῶμεν τῶν κατὰ τὴν ἐρμηνείαν πεφιλοπονημένων τισὶν τῶν λέξεων ἀδυ. ναμεῖν· οὐ γὰρ ἰσοδυναμεῖ αὐτὰ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Ἐβραιστὶ λεγόμενα καὶ ὅταν μεταχθῇ εἰς ἑτέραν γλῶσσαν· οὐ μόνον δὲ ταῦτα, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ νόμος καὶ αἱ προφητεῖαι καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν βιβλίων οὐ μικρὰν ἔχει τὴν διαφορὰν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λεγόμενα. ἐν γὰρ τῷ ὁγδόῳ καὶ τριακοστῷ ἔτει ἐπὶ τοῦ Εὐεργέτου βασιλέως παραγενηθεὶς εἰς Αἴγυπτον καὶ συνχρονίσας, εὑρον οὐ μικρᾶς παιδείας ἀφόμοιον. ἀναγκαιότατον ἐθέμην αὐτὸς προσενέγκασθαί τινα σπουδὴν καὶ φιλοπονίαν τοῦ μεθερμηνεῦσαι τήνδε τὴν βίβλον· πολλὴν γὰρ ἀγρυπνίαν καὶ ἐπιστήμην προσενεγκάμενος ἐν τῷ διαστῆματι τοῦ χρόνου πρὸς τὸ ἐπὶ πέρας ἄγοντα τὸ βιβλίον ἐκδοσθαι καὶ τοῖς ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ βουλομένοις φιλομαθεῖν, προκατασκευαζομένους τὰ ἤθη ἐν νόμῳ βιωτεύειν.

1.1: ΠΑΣA σοφία παρὰ Κυρίου, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
1.2: ἄμμον θαλασσῶν καὶ σταγόνας ὑετοῦ καὶ ἡμέρας αἰῶνος τίς ἐξαριθμήσει ;
1.3: ὕψος οὐρανοῦ καὶ πλάτος γῆς καὶ ἄβυσσον καὶ σοφίαυ τίς ἐξιχνιάσει ;
1.4: προτέρα πάντων ἔκτισται σοφία, καὶ σύνεσις φρονήσεως ἐξ αἰῶνυς.
1.6: ῥίζα σοφίας τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; καὶ τὰ πανουργεύματα αὐτῆς τίς ἔγνω;
1.7: εἷς ἐστὶν σοφός, φοβερὸς σφόδρα, καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ.
1.9: Κύριος ⁹αὐτὸς ἔκτισεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἴδεν καὶ ἐξηρίθμησεν αὐτήν, (10)καὶ ἐξέχεεν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ,
1.10: μετὰ πάσης σαρκὸς κατὰ τὴν δόσιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐχορήγησεν αὐτὴν τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
1.11: φόβος Κυρίου δόξα καὶ καύχημα καὶ εὐφροσύνη καὶ στέφανος ἀγαλλιάματος.
1.12: φόβος Κυρίου τέρψει καρδίαν, καὶ δώσει εὐφροσύνην καὶ χαρὰν καὶ μακροημέρευσιν. τῷ φοβουμένῳ τὸν κύριον εὖ ἔσται ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων, καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τελευτῆς αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει χάριν.
1.14: ἀρχὴ σοφίας φοβεῖσθαι τὸν θεόν, καὶ μετὰ πιστῶν ἐν μήτρᾳ συνεκτίσθη αὐτοῖς·
1.15: καὶ μετὰ ἀνθρώπων θεμέλιον αἰῶνος ἐνόσσευσεν, καὶ μετὰ τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῶν ἐμπιστευθήσεται.
1.16: πλησμονὴ σοφίας φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον. καὶ μεθύσκει αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῆς·
1.17: πάντα τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς ἐμπλήσει ἐπιθυμημάτων, καὶ τὰ ἀποδοχεῖα ἀπὸ τῶν γενημάτων αὐτῆς.
1.18: στέφανος σοφίας φόβος Κυρίου, ἀναθάλλων εἰρήνην καὶ ὑγείαν ἰάσεως.
1.19: καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐξηρίθμησεν αὐτήν, (24)ἐπιστήμην καὶ γνῶσιν συνέσεως ἐξώμβρησεν, καὶ δόξαν κρατούντων αὐτῆς ἀνύψωσεν.
1.20: ῥίζα σοφίας φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον. καὶ οἱ κλάδοι αὐτῆς μακροημέρευσις.
1.22: Οὐ δυνήσεται θυμὸς ἄδικος δικαιωθῆναι· ἡ γὰρ ῥοπὴ τοῦ θυμοῦ αὐτοῦ πτῶσις αὐτῷ.
1.23: ἕως καιροῦ ἀνθέξεται μακρόθυμος, καὶ ὕστερον αὐτῷ ἀναδώσει εὐφροσύνη·
1.24: ἕως καιροῦ κρύψει τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ, καὶ χείλη πιστῶν ἐκδιηγήσεται σύνεσιν αὐτοῦ.
1.25: ἐν θησαυροῖς σοφίας παραβολὴ· ἐπιστήμης, βδέλυγμα δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ θεοσέβεια.
1.26: ἐπιθυμήσας σοφίαν διατήρησον ἐντολάς, καὶ Κύριος χορηγήσει σοι αὐτήν.
1.27: σοφία γὰρ καὶ παιδεία φόβος Κυρίρυ, καὶ ἡ εὐδοκία αὐτοῦ (35)πίστις καὶ πρᾳότης.
1.28: μὴ ἀπειθήσῃς φόβῳ Κυρίου, καὶ μὴ προσέλθῃς αὐτῷ ἐν καρδίᾳ δισσῇ.
1.29: μὴ ὑποκριθῇς ἐν στόμασιν ἀνθρώπαν, καὶ ἐν τοῖς χείλεσίν σου πρόσεχε.
1.30: μὴ ἐξύψου σεαυτόν, ἵνα μὴ πέσῃς καὶ ἐπαγάγῃς· τῇ ψυχῇ σου ἀτιμίαν, (39)καὶ ἀποκαλύψει Κύριος τὰ κρυπτά σου. καὶ ἐν μέσῳ συναγωγῆς καταβαλεῖ σε, (40)ὅτι οὐ προσῆλθες φόβῳ Κυρίου, καὶ ἡ καρδία σου πλήρης δόλου.

2.1: Τέκνον, εἰ προσέρχῃ δουλεύειν Κυρίῳ θεῷ, ἑτοίμασον τὴν ψυχήν σου εἰς πειρασμόν·
2.2: εὔθυνον τὴν καρδίαν σου καὶ καρτέρησον, καὶ μὴ σπεύσῃς ἐν καιρῷ ἐπαγωγῆς·
2.3: κολλήθητι αὐτῷ καὶ μὴ ἀποστῇς, ἵνα αὐξηθῇς ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων σου.
2.4: πᾶν ὃ ἐὰν ἐπαχθῇ σοι δέξαι, καὶ ἐν ἀλλάγμασιν ταπεινώσεως σου μακροθύμησον·
2.5: ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ δοκιμάζεται χρυσός, καὶ ἄνθρωποι δεκτοὶ ἐν καμίνῳ ταπεινώσεαως.
2.6: πίστευσον αὐτῷ καὶ ἀντιλήμψεταί σου· εὔθυνον τὰς ὁδούς σου καὶ ἔλπισον ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
2.7: οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν κύριον, ἀναμείνατε τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ, καὶ μὴ ἐκκλινητε, ἵνα μὴ πέσητε.
2.8: οἱ φοβούμενοι Κύριον, πιστεύσατε αὐτῷ, καὶ οὐ μὴ πταίσῃ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν.
2.9: οἱ φοβούμενοι Κύριον, ἐλπίσατε εἰς ἀγαθὰ καὶ εἰς εὐφροσύυην αἰῶνος καὶ ἐλέους.
2.10: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς ἀρχαίας γενεὰς καὶ ἴδετε· τίς ἐνεπίστευσεν Κυρίῳ καὶ κατῃσχύνθη; (12)ἢ τίς ἐνέμεινεν τῷ φόβῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐγκατελείφθης ἢ τίς ἐπεκαλέσατο αὐτόν, καὶ ὑπερεῖδεν αὐτόν;
2.11: διότι οἰκτείρμων καὶ ἐλεήμων ὁ κύριρς, καὶ ἀφίησιν ἁμαρτίας καὶ σώζει ἐν καιρῷ θλίψεως.
2.12: οὐαὶ καρδίαις δειλαῖς καὶ χερσὶν παρειμέναις, καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἐπιβαίνοντι ἐπὶ δύο τρίβους.
2.13: οὐαὶ καρδίᾳ παρειμένῃ, ὅτι οὐ πιστεύει· διὰ τοῦτο οὐ σκεπασθήσεται.
2.14: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἀπολωλεκόσιν τὴν ὑπομονήν· καὶ τί ποιήσετε ὅταν ἐπισκέπτηται ὁ κύριος ;
2.15: οἱ φοβούμενοι Κύριον οὐκ ἀπειθήσουσνι ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ ἀγαπῶντες αὐτὸν συντηρήσουσιν τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ.
2.16: οἱ φοβούμενοι Κύριον ζητήσουσιν εὐδοκίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ ἀγαπῶντες αὐτὸν ἐμπλησθήσονται τοῦ νόμου.
2.17: οἱ φοβούμενοι Κύριον ἑτοιμάσουσιν καρδίας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ταπεινώσουσιν τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν.
2.18: ἐμπεσούμεθα εἰς χεῖρας Κυρίου καὶ οὐκ εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων· (23)ὡς γὰρ ἡ μεγαλωσύνη αὐτοῦ, οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ.

3.1: Ἐμοῦ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀκούσατε, τέκνα, καὶ οὕτως ποιήσατε, ἴνα σαωθῆτε.
3.2: ὁ γὰρ Κύριος ἐδόξασεν πατέρα ἐπὶ τέκνοις, καὶ κρίσιν μητρὸς ἐστερέωσεν ἐφʼ υἱοῖς.
3.3: ὁ τιμῶν πατέρα ἐξιλάσεται ἁμαρτίας·
3.4: καὶ ὡς ὁ ἀποθησαυρίζων ὁ δοξάζων μητέρα αὐτοῦ.
3.5: ὁ τιμῶν πατέρα εὐφρανθήσεται ὑπὸ τέκνων, καὶ ὡς ὁ ἀποθησαυρίζων ὁ δοξάζων μητέρα αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ προσευχῆς αὐτοῦ εἰσακουσθήσεται.
3.6: ὁ δοξάζων πατέρα μακροημερεύσει, καὶ ὁ εἰσακούων Κυρίου ἀναπαύσει μητέρα αὐτοῦ,
3.7: καὶ ὡς δεσπόταις δουλεύσει ἐν τοῖς γεννήσασιν αὐτόν.
3.8: ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου, (10)ἵνα ἐπέλθῃ σοι εὐλογία παρʼ αὐτοῦ·
3.9: εὐλογία γὰρ πατρὸς στηρίζει οἴκους τέκνων, κατάρα δέ μητρὸς ἐκριζοῖ θεμέλια.
3.10: μὴ δοξάζου ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ πατρός σου, οὐ γάρ ἐστίν σοι δόξα πρὸς ἀτιμίαν·
3.11: ἡ γὰρ δόξα ἀνθρώπου ἐκ τιμῆς πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὄνειδος τέκνοις μήτηρ ἐν ἀδοξίᾳ.
3.12: τέκνον, ἀντιλαβοῦ ἐν γήρᾳ πατρός σου, καὶ μὴ λυπήσῃς αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·
3.13: κἂν ἀπολείπῃ σύνεσιν, συγγνώμην ἔχε, καὶ μὴ ἀτιμάσῃς αὐτὸν ἐν πάσῃ ἰσχύι σου.
3.14: ἐλεημοσύνη γὰρ πατρὸς οὐκ ἐπιλησθήσεται, (16) καὶ ἀντὶ ἁμαρτιῶν (17)προσανοικοδομηθήσεταί σοι·
3.15: ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως σου ἀναμνησθήσεταί σου· ὡς εὐδία ἐπὶ παγετῷ, οὕτως ἀναλυθήσονταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
3.16: ὡς βλάσφημος ὁ ἐγκαταλιπὼν πατέρα, καὶ κεκατηραμένος ὑπὸ Κυρίου ὁ παροργίζων μητέρα αὐτοῦ.
3.17: Τέκνον, ἐν πρᾳύτητι τὰ ἔργα σου διέξαγε, καὶ ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπου δεκτοῦ ἀγαπηθήσῃ.
3.18: ὅσῳ μέγας εἰ, τοσούτῳ ταπεινοῦ σεαυτόν, καὶ ἔναντι Κυρίου εὑρήσεις χάριν·
3.20: ὅτι μεγάλη ἡ δυναστεία τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ταπεινῶν δοξάζεται.
3.21: χαλεπώτερά σου μὴ ζήτει. καὶ ἰσχυρότερά σου μὴ ἐξέταζε.
3.22: ἃ προσετάγη σοι, ταῦτα διανοοῦ· (23)οὐ γάρ ἐστίν σοι χρεία τῶν κρυπτῶν.
3.23: ἐν τοῖς περισσοῖς τῶν ἔργων σου μὴ περιεργάζου· (25) πλείονα γὰρ συνέσεως ἀνθρώπων ὑπεδείχθη σοι.
3.25: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐπλάνησεν ἡ ὑπόλημψις αὐτῶν, καὶ ὑπόνοια πονηρὰ ὠλίσθησεν διανοίας αὐτῶν.
3.26: καὶ ὁ ἀγαπῶν κίνδυνον ἐν αὐτῷ ἐμπεσεῖται· καρδία σκληρὰ κακωθήσεται ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων, καρδία σκληρὰ βαρυνθήσεται ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων.
3.27: καρδία σκληρὰ βαρυνθήσεται πόνοις, καὶ ὁ ἁμαρταυλὸς προσθήσει ἁμαρτίαν ἐφʼ ἁμαρτίαις.
3.28: ἐπαγωγῇ ὑπερηφάνου οὐκ ἔστιν ἴασις, φυτὸν γὰρ πονηρίας ἐρρίζωκεν ἐν αὐτῷ.
3.29: καρδία συνετοῦ διανοηθήσεται παραβολήν, καὶ οὖς ἀκροατοῦ ἐπιθυμία σοφοῦ.
3.30: πῦρ φλογιζόμενον ἀποσβέσει ὕδωρ, καὶ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐξιλάσεται ἁμαρτίας.
3.31: ὁ ἀνταποδιδοὺς χάριτας μέμνηται εἰς τὰ μετὰ ταῦτα, καὶ ἐν καιρῷ πτώσεαως εὑρήσει στήριγμα.

4.1: Τέκνον, τὴν ζωὴν τοῦ πτωχοῦ μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, καὶ μὴ παρελκύσῃς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπιδεεῖς.
4.2: ψυχὴν πεινῶσαν μὴ λυπήσῃς, καὶ μὴ παροργίσῃς ἄνδρα ἐν ἀπορίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
4.3: καρδίαν παροργισμένην μὴ προσταράξῃς, καὶ μὴ παρελκύσῃς δόσιν προσδεομένου.
4.4: ἱκέτην θλιβόμενον μὴ ἀπαναίνου, καὶ μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς τὸ πρόσαωπόν σου ἀπὸ πτωχοῦ.
4.5: ἀπὸ δεομένου μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς ὀφθαλμόν, καὶ μὴ δῷς τόπον ἀνθρώπῳ καταράσασθαί σε·
4.6: καταραωμένου γάρ σε ἐν πικρίᾳ ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ, τῆς δεήσεως αὐτοῦ ἐπακούσεται ὁ ποιήσας αὐτόν.
4.7: προσφιλῆ συναγωγῇ σεαυτὸν ποίει, καὶ μεγιστᾶνι ταπείνου τὴν κεφαλήν σου.
4.8: κλῖνον πτωχῷ τὸ οὖς σου, καὶ ἀποκρίθητι αὐτῷ εἰρηνικὰ ἐν πρᾳύτητι.
4.9: ἐξελοῦ ἀδικούμενον ἐκ χειρὸς ἀδικοῦντος, καὶ μὴ ὀλιγοψυχήσῃς ἐν τῷ κρίνειν σε.
4.10: γίνου ὀρφανοῖς ὡς πατήρ, καὶ ἀντὶ ἀνδρὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῶν· (11)καὶ ἔσῃ ὡς υἱὸς Ὑψίστου, καὶ ἀγαπήσει σε μᾶλλον ἢ μήτηρ σου.
4.11: Ἡ σοφία υἱοὺς ἑαυτῇ ἀνύψωσεν, καὶ ἐπιλαμβάνεται τῶν ζητούντων αὐτήν.
4.12: ὁ ἀγαπῶν αὐτὴν ἀγαπᾷ ζωήν, καὶ οἱ ὀρθρίζοντες πρὸς αὐτὴν ἐμπλησθήσονται εὐφροσύνης·
4.13: ὁ κρατῶν αὐτῆς κληρονομήσει δόξαν, καὶ οὗ εἰσπορεύεται, εὐλογήσει Κύριος·
4.14: οἱ λατρεύοντες αὐτῇ λειτουργήσουσιν ἁγίῳ, καὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτὴν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κύριος·
4.15: ὁ ὑπακούων αὐτῆς κρινεῖ ἔθνη, καὶ ὁ προσελθὼν αὐτῇ κατασκηνώσει πεποιθώς.
4.16: ἐὰν ἐμπιστεύσῃς, κατακληρονομήσεις αὐτήν, καὶ ἐν κατασχέσει ἔσονται αἱ γενεαὶ αὐτοῦ·
4.17: ὅτι διεστραμμένως πορεύεται μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν πρώτοις, (19)φόβον δὲ καὶ δειλίαν ἐπάξει ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ βασανίσει αὐτὸν ἐν παιδίᾳ αὐτῆς, ἕως οὗ ἐνπιστεύσῃ τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ· καὶ πειράσει αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς δικαιώμασιν αὐτῆς·
4.18: καὶ πάλιν ἐπανήξει κατʼ εὐθεῖαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εὐφρανεῖ αὐτόν, (21)καὶ ἀποκαλύψει αὐτῷ τὰ κρυπτὰ αὐτῆς.
4.19: ἐὰν ἀποπλανηθῇ, ἐγκαταλείψει αὐτόν, καὶ παραδώσει αὐτὸν εἰς χεῖρας πτώσεως αὐτοῦ.
4.20: Συντήρησον καιρὸν καὶ φύλαξαι ἀπὸ πονηροῦ, (²⁴)καὶ περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς σου μὴ αἰσχυνθῇς·
4.21: ἔστιν γὰρ αἰσχύνη ἐπάγουσα ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ ἔστιν αἰσχύνη δόξα καὶ χάρις.
4.22: μὴ λάβῃς πρόσωπον κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς σου, (27)καὶ μὴ ἐντραπῇς εἰς πτῶσίν σου.
4.23: μὴ κωλύσῃς λόγον ἐν καιρῷ σωτηρίας·
4.24: ἐν γὰρ λόγῳ γνωσθήσεται σοφία, καὶ παιδεία ἐν ῥήματι γλώσσης.
4.25: μὴ ἀντίλεγε τῆ ἀληθεία, καὶ περὶ τῆς ἀπαιδευσίας σου ἐντράπητι·
4.26: μὴ αἰσχυνθῇς ὁμολογῆσαι ἐφʼ ἁμαρτίαις σου, (32)καὶ μὴ βιάζου ῥοῦν ποταμοῦ.
4.27: καὶ μὴ ὑποστρώσῃς σεαυτὸν ἀνθρώπῳ μωρῷ, καὶ μὴ λάβῃς πρόσωπον δυνάστου.
4.28: ἕως τοῦ θανάτου ἀγώνισαι περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας, καὶ Κύριος ὁ θεὸς πολεμήσει ὑπέρ σοῦ.
4.29: μὴ γίνου τραχὺς ἐν γλώσσῃ σου, καὶ νωθρὸς καὶ παρειμένος ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις σου.
4.30: μὴ ἴσθι ὡς λέων ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου, καὶ φαντασιοκοπῶυ ἐν τοῖς οἰκέταις σου.
4.31: μὴ ἔστω ἡ χείρ σου ἐκτεταμένη εἰς τὸ λαβεῖν, καὶ ἐν τῷ ἀποδιδόναι συνεσταλμένη.

5.1: μὴ ἔπεχε ἐπὶ τοῖς χρήμασίν σου, καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς Αὐτάρκη μοί ἐστιν.
5.2: μὴ ἐξακολούθει τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ τῇ ἰσχύι σου, πορεύεσθαι ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις καρδίας σου·
5.3: καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς Τίς με δυναστεύσει; ὁ γὰρ κύριος ἐκδικῶν ἐκδικήσει σε.
5.4: μὴ εἴπῃς Ἥμαρτον, καὶ τί μοι ἐγένετο ; ὁ γὰρ κύριός ἐστιν μακρόθυμος.
5.5: περὶ ἐξιλασμοῦ μὴ ἄφοβος γίνου. προσθεῖναι ἁμαρτίαν ἐφʼ ἁμαρτίαις·
5.6: καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς Ο οἰκτειρμὸς αὐτοῦ πολύς, τὸ πλῆθος τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν μου ἐξιλάσεται· (7)ἔλεος γὰρ καὶ ὀργὴ παρʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπὶ ἁμαρτωλοὺς καταπαύσει ὁ θυμὸς αὐτοῦ·
5.7: μὴ ἀνάμενε ἐπιστρέψαι πρὸς Κύριον, καὶ μὴ ὑπερβάλλου ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας· (9)ἐξάπινα γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται ὀργὴ Κυρίου. καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἐκδικήσεως ἐξολῇ.
5.8: μὴ ἔπεχε ἐπὶ χρήμασιν ἀδίκοις· οὐδὲν γὰρ ὠφελήσεις ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπαγωγῆς
5.9: μὴ λίκμα ἐν παντὶ ἀνέμῳ, καὶ μὴ πορεύου ἐν πάσῃ ἀτραπῷ· οὕτως ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς ὁ δίγλωσσος.
5.10: ἵσθι ἐστηριγμένος ἐν συνέσει σου, καὶ εἷς ἔστω σου ὁ λόγος.
5.11: γίνου ταχὺς ἐν ἀκροάσει σου, καὶ ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ φθέγγου ἀπόκρισιν.
5.12: εἰ ἔστιν σοι σύνεσις, ἀποκρίθητι τῷ πλησίον· εἰ δὲ μή, ἡ χείρ σου ἔστω ἐπὶ στόματί σου.
5.13: δόξα καὶ ἀτιμία ἐν λαλιᾷ, καὶ γλῶσσα ἀνθρώπου πτῶσις αὐτῷ.
5.14: μὴ κληθῇς ψίθυρος, καὶ τῇ γλώσσῃ σου μὴ ἐνεδρευθῇς· (17)ἐπὶ γὰρ τῷ κλέπτῃ ἐστὶν αἰσχύνη, καὶ κατάγνωσις πονηρὰ ἐπὶ διγλώσσου.
5.15: ἐν μεγάλῳ καὶ ἐν μικρῷ μὴ ἀγνόει,

6.1: καὶ ἀντὶ φίλου μὴ γίνου ἐχθρός· ὄνομα γὰρ πονηρὸν αἰσχύνη, καὶ ὄνειδος κληρονομήσει· οὕτως ὁ ἁμαρτωλὸς ὁ δίγλωσσος.
6.2: μὴ ἐπάρῃς σεαυτὸν ἐν βουλῇ ψυχῆς σου, ἵνα μὴ διαρπαγῇ ὡς ταῦρος ἡ ψυχή σου·
6.3: τὰ φύλλα σου καταφάγεσαι καὶ τοὺς καρποὺς σου ἀπολέσεις, καὶ ἀφήσεις σεαυτὸν ὡς ξύλον ξηρόν.
6.4: Ψυχὴ πονηρὰ ἀπολεῖ τὸν κτησάμενον αὐτήν, καὶ ἐπίχαρμα ἐχθρῶν ποιήσει αὐτόν.
6.5: λάρυγξ γλυκὺς πληθυνεῖ φίλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ γλῶσσα εὔλαλος πληθυνεῖ εὐπροσήγορα.
6.6: οἱ εἰρηνεύοντές σοι ἔστωσαν πολλοί, οἱ δὲ σύμβουλοί σου εἰς ἀπὸ χιλίων.
6.7: εἰ κτᾶσαι φίλον, ἐν πειρασμῷ κτῆσαι αὐτόν, καὶ μὴ ταχὺ ἐμπιστεύσῃς αὐτῷ.
6.8: ἔστιν γὰρ φίλος ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ μὴ παραμείνῃ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως σου·
6.9: καὶ ἔστιν φίλος μετατιθέμενος εἰς ἔχθραν, καὶ μάχην ὀνειδισμοῦ σου ἀποκαλύψει·
6.10: καὶ ἔστιν φίλος κοινωνὸς τραπεζῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ παραμείνῃ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεώς σου·
